RPO (recovery point objective) How much recent data or records can be lost, where that applies. Optional. Gap Something in the plan that the live records show is not true or not covered. High gaps are in red. What the statuses mean Status Meaning Draft Being written. Dependencies and scenarios can be edited. In review Sent to the plant manager for approval. Approved In force. Exercises can be scheduled. The call list can still be edited. Superseded Replaced by a newer revision. Kept for history. Write a plan Click New continuity plan . Choose the site and criticality. Enter the RTO (hours) , optionally the RPO, and an alternate owner (someone other than you who can act if you are away). Name the Critical process , for example "stamping of HSG-220 housings", and give the plan a title. Click Create . On the plan, click Edit plan under Dependencies . Add each thing the process depends on: equipment, a supplier, a skill (qualification), a person, or something else (a utility, IT, a building). For each, say what the process needs from it and what the workaround is. For a skill, say how many holders you need (two unless you change it); the plan will flag it if fewer hold the qualification at the site. Under Scenarios and recovery , add each disruption (press breakdown, supplier fails, site inaccessible): its impact, the recovery steps in order, the recovery owner, the estimated recovery hours, and optionally a controlled procedure from Document control . A scenario whose estimate is above the RTO is marked Over RTO . Click Save plan . Click Edit call list and add the people to call: name, role, and a phone or an email. Click Send for plant manager approval . It needs at least one scenario with recovery steps and a call list. Gaps do not block approval; they stay visible. Gaps The Gaps box is worked out live each time you open the plan. It checks qualification holders at the site against what the plan needs, employee and supplier status, sole-source parts, the state of equipment, and whether reviews and exercises are up to date. For example: only one person holds a needed qualification, a listed supplier is inactive, a machine is down, an exercise is overdue, or the RTO has not been shown by a timed exercise. Fix the cause (train a second person, line up another supplier) or add an action. Exercises A plan only counts as ready once it has been tested. Once the plan is approved, schedule exercises. Kind What it is Timed? Tabletop People talk through the scenario. No Walkthrough People walk through the steps in place. No Simulation A realistic run of the recovery. Yes: record how long recovery took. Full test The recovery actually performed. Yes: record how long recovery took. Click Schedule exercise . Choose the kind, a scenario (or the whole plan), the date and the facilitator. Click Schedule . After it happens, the facilitator, the owner or a manager clicks Record result . Enter the date it took place (not in the future), who took part, and the outcome: Objectives met , Partly met or Not met . For a simulation or full test, enter Recovery took (hours) . If it is longer than the RTO, the exercise cannot count as met. Write the findings (required unless the objectives were met). Click Record result . If the outcome was not met, add an action from the exercise row with + action . Click Evidence to attach sign-in sheets, timings or photos. Results are final once recorded. Check them before you save. The tile Recovered in (timed exercise) shows the recovery time only if a simulation or full test finished within the RTO. Otherwise it shows "Not shown", with the best timed result as a note. Tabletops and walkthroughs never demonstrate an RTO. Actions Click Add action to give a follow-up to someone, with a due date. Owners and managers click Mark done and say what was done. Overdue actions are marked, and appear on the owner's My actions tab (see Quality ). Review and revise An approved plan has a review date, set from the plan's review interval, and an exercise interval. Both intervals are shown under Review and revision . To confirm the plan is still right, type what you checked (contacts called, dependencies still current) in Review note and click Confirm review . The next review date moves forward. To change it, type why under Why revise (exercise findings, new equipment, supplier change) and click Start revision N . A new draft revision opens. It must be approved again, and when it is, the old one is superseded. Only the call list can be edited on an approved plan; changes apply at once and are writte

title: Conditions and visits
text: This page has two jobs for sites that must prove they keep standards: condition logs (temperature or similar readings from coolers, freezers and other equipment, checked against limits) and site visits (a manager walks a site with a checklist, and each failed item turns into a repair request or a task). It is used by retail, food service and property sites, and by any plant with a cooler or a clean room to watch. See conditions and visits : store and site managers, district managers, facilities and property managers, quality managers, technicians and executives (permission "view visits"). Log a reading : people who can record equipment state at the site (technicians, operators, store managers and others; permission "record equipment state"). Set the limits on a piece of equipment : asset managers (permission "manage assets"), from the equipment's page. Conduct a visit and manage the checklists : people with "conduct site visits", typically store/site managers, facilities and property managers and plant managers. Open Quality & safety → Conditions & visits . The tabs are Conditions , Visits and, for people who conduct visits, Checklists . Conditions: readings against limits The Conditions tab lists every logged point, with the site, the equipment, its limits (and how often it should be read), the last reading, and its state. Tiles show how many points are logged, how many are out of limits now, and how many readings are overdue. Rows that are not OK are highlighted. State Meaning ok The last reading is within limits and a reading is not overdue. out since … The last reading is outside the limits. The worst value of the excursion is shown in red. missed No reading for one and a half times the expected interval. no readings Set up but nothing logged yet. Log a reading Find the equipment's row. (You can also scan the equipment's QR code to land on its page; the same form is there.) Type the value in the box, using the unit shown. Optionally add a Note / action taken . Click Log . A message tells you the result. If the value is outside the limits, an excursion opens and one maintenance request is raised and maintenance managers are told: "Out of limits: maintenance has been asked to check it." A cooler that stays warm for six readings raises one request, not six; further readings are added to the same excursion. When a reading is back inside the limits, the excursion closes. See Work orders for what maintenance does with the request. Set up limits Open the cooler or freezer from Maintenance → Assets (see Assets ). In the Condition log box, click Log temperature (or Edit limits ). Enter the unit (°F, °C, %RH), a low limit, a high limit (one or both; low must be below high), and how many hours between readings. Click Save . The asset page also shows the last seven days of readings and recent excursions, including the worst value and the maintenance work order. Visits: walking a site with a checklist The Visits tab lists past visits with the site, checklist, date, who visited, the score and the number of open fixes. A visit with a critical failure is highlighted. Do a visit On the Visits tab choose the Site and the Checklist , then click Start visit . The visit keeps its own copy of the checklist, so changing the checklist later does not alter it. Go through the items. Each shows its area. A critical tag marks an item that matters most. A failed last time too tag marks a repeat failure. For a good item click Pass . If it does not apply, click n/a . For a failure, type what is wrong in If it fails: what is wrong (required). If it is about a piece of equipment or a space, pick it in the list. Otherwise leave Not equipment (an action) . Then click Fail . To change an answer before you finish, click change . When every item is answered, add a Summary for the store . If any failed item was not about equipment, choose Who fixes the rest… . Click Complete visit . What happens when you complete the visit: The score is passes divided by passes plus failures. "n/a" items are left out. The score and the number of critical failures show on the visit and on the list. Each failure about equipment or a space becomes a maintenance request (high severity if the item is critical, otherwise medium). Each other failure becomes an action for the person you chose, due the next day if critical, otherwise in a week. It appears on their My actions tab (see Quality ). If anything failed, the people at the site who can request work orders are told, with the score and the first failures. The visit page shows the previous visit's score for comparison, and each failed item shows its follow-up: the maintenance request or work order, or the action's status. Checklists People who conduct visits can create and edit checklists on the Checklists tab. Click New checklist (or Edit on an existing one). Give it a short Code and a Name . Type one item per line, written as Area: item . Start a line with ! to mark it critical. For example: Front: Entrance clean and doors working ! Cold chain: Coolers in range, logs complete Click Save checklist . A checklist needs at least one item. The list shows how many items each checklist has and how many are critical. Common mistakes Logging nothing, then everything at once. Missed readings are flagged. Read at the interval set for the equipment. Not writing what is wrong. A failed item can't be saved without a note, and the note becomes the repair request. Failing equipment without picking it. If you don't pick the equipment, the failure becomes an action for a person, not a maintenance request. Waiting to start the visit until you are back in the office. Do it as you walk; a tablet works. Visits and condition logs are part of the Standard edition and can be switched off or limited by role. Two reminders support them: "Missed condition readings" and "Store walks not done" (default: a site with walks and none completed in 31 days). Give the visit and record-state per

title: Customers
text: The customer record is where sales work starts. It holds the account details, the people you deal with, the deals you are chasing and a log of every call and email. Quotes, orders and invoices all hang off a customer, so a clean record here saves time everywhere else. See customers, the pipeline and follow-ups : sales representatives and managers, bookkeepers, billing clerks, finance approvers, plant managers, quality managers, executives, dispatchers and field technicians (permission "view customers"). Add or change customers, contacts, opportunities and activities : sales representatives, sales managers and bookkeepers (permission "manage customers"). Start a quote from a customer : sales representatives, sales managers and service dispatchers (permission "quote"). Find a customer Open Sales & supply → Customers . The page has three tabs: Customers , Pipeline and My follow-ups . On Customers , type part of a name or code into Search . Each row shows the code, name, type, industry, owner, how many opportunities are open and the date of the last activity. Click a row to open the customer. Type What it means Prospect Someone you are talking to who has not bought yet. Every new customer you add by hand starts here. Customer A prospect that has accepted a quote. The record changes to Customer by itself when you record the acceptance (see Quotes and orders ). Add a customer On the Customers page, click New customer . You only see the button if you can manage customers. Enter a Code (a short unique label such as ACME) and the Name . Both are required. Fill in Industry , Phone , Website and Billing address if you have them. Payment terms starts as Net 30 ; change it if this customer has different terms. New invoices and quotes take their terms from here. Click Save customer . The new record opens. If you already keep a customer list in a spreadsheet or another system, ask your administrator to bring it in with Data import instead of typing each one. See Importing data . Contacts, opportunities and activity The customer page is laid out in blocks. If you can manage customers, each block has a small form under its table. Contacts Under Contacts , enter the person's name (required), and optionally title, email and phone. Tick Primary for the person who should receive invoices and payment reminders. The reminder email on a receivable goes to the primary contact's email. Click Add contact . Opportunities An opportunity is a possible sale: a title, an amount, and the date you expect to close it. Under Opportunities , type a title (at least three letters), an amount and an expected close date. Click Add . It starts at the Lead stage. As the deal moves, pick the next stage in the row and click Move . If you choose Lost , type why in the Why lost? box. Stage Starting chance of winning Lead 10% Qualified 25% Proposal 50% Negotiation 75% Won 100% Lost 0% When you accept a quote that is linked to an opportunity, the opportunity moves to Won by itself. Won and lost opportunities no longer show a stage selector. Activity Use Activity to keep a record of what happened. Choose the kind ( Call , Email , Meeting , Note or Follow-up task ), write a short summary and click Log . A follow-up task also needs a due date. If the customer has an open opportunity you can tie the entry to it. The pipeline The Pipeline tab lists all open opportunities in four columns: Lead, Qualified, Proposal and Negotiation. The line above the columns shows how many are open, the total value, and the value weighted by probability : each amount multiplied by its chance of winning. Click a card to open its customer. My follow-ups The My follow-ups tab lists your open follow-up tasks with their due dates. Overdue ones have a red edge. Click Done when you have finished one. The task owner is also reminded when a follow-up falls due. Other things on the customer page Quotes and orders : lists of this customer's quotes and sales orders (Standard edition only). Click one to open it. New quote in the page header starts a quote for this customer. Specifications : if your company stores this customer's drawings or standards in document control, they are listed here with the revision currently in force. See Document control . Account : open invoices, payments, credit limit and exposure are on the customer's account page under Receivables. See Receivables . Lite and Standard Customers, contacts, opportunities and follow-ups work the same in both editions. In the Lite edition the quote and order blocks do not appear, because quotes, sales orders and shipments are part of Standard. Common mistakes Duplicate customers. Search by name before adding. Two records for the same company split their invoices and credit exposure. No primary contact. Without one, the Email payment reminder button on an invoice is unavailable. Forgetting to log a lost reason. The reason is the only record of why you did not win the work. Administrators can import customer lists and set credit limits and owners in bulk. Roles that may manage customers are set per role; see Roles and access and Importing data .

title: Quotes and orders
text: A quote is your written price to a customer. When the customer accepts it, you record that acceptance and the system turns the quote into a sales order. You then ship the order and invoice what shipped. This page walks through each step and what the statuses mean. Quotes, orders and shipments are part of the Standard edition. The Lite edition has customers and invoices but no quotes or orders. See quotes and orders : sales representatives and managers, plant managers, quality managers, finance approvers, billing clerks, bookkeepers, executives (permission "view sales"). Build, finish, send, revise, extend and record acceptance of quotes : sales representatives, sales managers and service dispatchers (permission "quote"). This is checked for the selling site. Add catalog items, set a promise date, ship, make : sales managers and plant or operations managers (permission "manage orders"). Approve out-of-limit pricing : the sales manager role, from the Approvals page. Release a credit hold : finance approvers (permission "release credit holds"). The sales catalog Open Sales & supply → Quotes & orders and click the Catalog tab. It lists the products and services you sell with their list price and standard cost. If you can manage orders, add one with the form under the table: code, description, Product or Service , list price, standard cost and, for a stocked product, the part it ships from. Quote lines can pick catalog items, which brings in the list price and cost so the system can check discount and margin. Build a quote Open the customer ( Customers ) and click New quote . You can also arrive here from a customer request ( Customer requests for quote ). Choose the Customer , enter a Title (at least three letters) and pick a Contact and, if one applies, an Opportunity . Choose the Selling site . Only sites where you may quote are offered. Set Valid until . If you leave it empty the quote is valid for 30 days from today. Under Lines , choose a catalog item or Not in the catalog (describe it) , then enter quantity and unit price. Leave the price empty to use the list price. A badge shows how far below list a line is. Click Add a line for more. Under Terms shown to the customer , fill in Lead time , Delivery , Included and Not included . Add Notes shown on the quote if needed. Click Save draft . Use Preview PDF on the next page to see the letter. The quote prints as a one-page letter with a validity banner, your terms, a signature block and page footers. Prices are stated excluding taxes. Tax and freight are not quote lines; they are added on the order's invoice. You can edit lines and terms while the quote is a draft ( Edit lines , Edit terms shown to the customer ). Once it has been finished, change it by making a new revision. Finish, approve and send On the quote, click Finish quote . The system checks the pricing. If every line is within 15% of list price and the margin on costed lines is at least 20%, the quote is ready to send. Otherwise a banner explains why, and the quote goes to a sales manager for Pricing approval . The manager decides from the Approvals page ( Home and approvals ). When the status is Ready to send , type the recipient in Send to (it defaults to the contact's email) and click Mark as sent (stores the PDF) . The system does not email the quote. Mark as sent freezes that revision, stores the exact PDF and logs the send on the customer. Open the PDF from the Sent table and send it yourself. The stored PDF is never changed afterward. Quote statuses Status Meaning What you can do Draft Being written. Edit lines and terms, then finish it. Pricing approval Outside the discount or margin limits; waiting for a sales manager. Wait, or start a new revision. Ready to send Pricing is cleared. Mark as sent, extend validity, or revise. Sent The customer has the PDF. Record acceptance or a decline, extend validity, or revise. Accepted The customer said yes; an order exists. Open the order. Declined The customer said no; the reason is kept. Start a new revision if they come back. Cancelled No longer going ahead. Nothing. Validity and expiry A red Expired badge appears next to a ready or sent quote whose Valid until date has passed. Expiry is worked out from the date; it is not a separate status. An expired quote cannot be accepted . Extend it or revise it first. On the quote list, the Validity filter shows Expiring within 7 days or Expired , and Time left counts the days. The quote owner is reminded 7 days before, 2 days before, and the day after a sent quote's expiry. Sent quotes that expired with no decision also appear on What is late . Extend a quote's validity On a quote that is Ready to send or Sent , set Extend validity to a date later than the current one. Type a Reason , such as "customer's budget approval pending". Click Extend . The old date, new date, reason, who and when are kept in Validity history , together with the original date. The PDF you already sent does not change; the customer's copy still shows the old date, so tell them in writing. Record the customer's acceptance When the customer says yes, open the sent quote. Under Record the customer's acceptance enter Accepted by (name) and Their title . Choose How they accepted : Purchase order , Signed quote , Email , Verbal or Customer portal . Set Date accepted . It cannot be in the future or before the quote was sent. Enter the Customer PO number . It is required when the method is Purchase order . Add a Note if they said something worth keeping, such as "ship in two lots". Click Customer accepted: create order . Then scan or upload the signed quote or PO under Files on the same page. The system records who, how, when, the revision and the total that was accepted, and creates the sales order from that revision. The opportunity moves to Won and the customer record becomes a customer. If the customer says no, type a reason in the box and click Customer declined . Revise a quote Type what changes in the Reason b

title: Customer requests for quote
text: Customers often send a request for quote (an RFQ) by email with drawings or a spec attached. This page is where you log each one, so the reply date is visible to the whole sales team and nothing is forgotten. You then decide whether to bid, build the quote from the request, and let the status follow the quote. The platform does not read your email. You record each request by hand when it arrives. It is part of the Standard edition, together with quotes and orders. See requests and the due board : anyone who can view sales (sales representatives and managers, plant managers, quality managers, finance approvers, billing clerks, bookkeepers, executives). Record, decide, build the quote, change the date, close a request : sales representatives, sales managers and service dispatchers (permission "quote"), for their own site. The list and the due board Open Sales & supply → Quotes & orders and click the Customer requests tab. Four tiles at the top count requests by reply date: Past the reply date Due today Due in 7 days Waiting for bid or no-bid : requests nobody has decided on yet. The table lists each request with the customer, their reference, the subject, the date a reply is due, the days left, the owner and the status. Late rows have a red edge. Tick Only open requests to hide finished ones. Record a request On the Customer requests tab, click Record a request . Choose the Customer and, if you know who sent it, the Contact . Type Their reference (the customer's own RFQ number) so you can quote it back to them. Choose How it arrived : email, portal, phone, meeting or other. Set Received on and Reply due by . The reply date cannot be earlier than the received date. Choose the Quoting site . Enter a Subject (at least three letters) and describe What they are asking for . Click Record request . On the next page, add the files the customer sent under Files from the customer . You become the owner of the request. The owner receives the reminders. Decide and answer Open a request. The tiles show the reply date, when it arrived, the owner and the linked quote. While the request is open, the What to do block offers these actions. To commit, click We will bid . The status changes to Bidding . To decline, type a Reason (at least three letters) and click No bid . The reason is required so you can later see patterns such as too small, outside our range or no capacity. To answer with a price, click Build the quote . The quote form opens with the customer already chosen. Enter lines, validity and notes as described in Quotes and orders and click Save draft . The request is now linked to that quote and moves to Bidding if it was not already. The button then reads Quote already started . If the customer takes the request back, type a reason and click Customer withdrew it . If the reply date moves, pick the new date under Move the reply date and click Change date . You do not set Quoted , Won or Lost yourself. They follow the quote, so the outcome is only entered once. What the statuses mean Status Meaning Needs a decision Recorded; nobody has chosen to bid or not. Bidding You decided to bid, or a quote has been started but not yet sent. No bid You chose not to quote. The reason is kept. Quoted The linked quote has been sent to the customer. Won The linked quote was accepted. Lost The linked quote was declined. Withdrawn The customer withdrew the request. Reply late (red badge) The reply date has passed while the request is still Needs a decision or Bidding . Reminders and what is late Every morning the owner of each open request is told two days before the reply date, on the day, and every day after it until the request is answered or closed. Requests past their date also appear on What is late . The report Customer quote requests in Reports shows reply times across all requests. Common mistakes Leaving a request at "Needs a decision". Decide quickly. A request nobody has decided on is the most likely to be missed. Building the quote outside the request. Start it with Build the quote so the two stay linked and the status updates itself. Forgetting the customer's reference. Without it, reconciling your reply to their system is harder. Customer requests are recorded by hand; there is no email intake until your company chooses a sending and receiving domain. Reminders go to the request owner by the daily job; see Scheduled jobs and Reminders and retention .

title: Purchasing
text: Purchasing follows one path: someone raises a purchase request , the right people approve it, a buyer turns it into a purchase order , the delivery is received , and the supplier's invoice is checked against the order and what actually arrived. That last check is called a three-way match: order, receipt and invoice must agree. Purchasing is part of the Standard edition. The Lite edition has suppliers and bills but no purchase requests, orders or receiving; bills are entered without an order (see Payables ). See requests, orders, suppliers and supplier performance : buyers, plant and maintenance managers, technicians, quality managers, finance approvers, executives and others (permission "view purchasing"). Raise a purchase request : technicians, maintenance and plant managers, supervisors, buyers (permission "request purchases"). Place orders, add suppliers and supplier prices, cancel orders, run quote requests : buyers (permission "manage purchasing"). Receive deliveries : buyers and maintenance managers (permission "receive goods"). Approve a request : whoever the sign-off route names, from the Approvals page. Raise a purchase request Open Sales & supply → Purchasing and click New request . Choose the Facility , give it a Title (at least three letters), and set the Spend type : Operating (repairs, consumables) or Capital (asset, improvement) . Optionally set Needed by and explain Why is this needed? Under Lines , choose a catalog part or describe something that is not a catalog part. Enter the quantity, the unit if it is not the part's stock unit, an estimated unit price and, if you know it, the supplier and the storeroom it goes into. For a catalog part, leaving the supplier empty means its preferred supplier; for a described item the buyer decides. Click Save draft . On the next screen, check the Sign-off route shown for the total, then click Submit for approval . Every line needs an estimated price first. To restock, choose a facility next to Draft from reorder report on the Requests tab. It drafts a request for the parts below their reorder point. A request can also start from a work order that needs parts. Request statuses Status Meaning Draft Still being written. Edit it freely, then submit. Awaiting approval Signed off step by step; the route and who has signed are under Sign-offs . Approved All sign-offs are in. A buyer can now order it. Rejected A signer said no. Change the request and resubmit. Ordered Every line is on a purchase order. Cancelled Cancelled by the requester or a buyer, with a reason. If you edit lines after the request has been submitted, the sign-offs are voided and the request goes back to draft. It must be approved again. The requester and buyers can cancel a request that has no orders yet: type a reason (at least three letters) and click Cancel request . Place the order Open an Approved request. If you can manage purchasing, the Place the order block appears. Check each line's Order price . You can change it to the price the supplier actually quoted. The block shows how many purchase orders will be created: one per supplier. Optionally set Expected delivery . If you leave it empty, the system uses the supplier's lead time for the part, or the request's needed-by date. Click Create purchase order . Orders may come in up to 10% above the approved amount. Beyond that, edit the request so it goes back for approval. A line with no supplier shows a Choose a supplier… box in the Place the order block: pick an active supplier there. The choice is kept on the line and recorded in the audit trail, and it does not change the approved amount; orders are then created one per supplier. A line left without a supplier cannot be ordered, and the system tells you which one. Choosing suppliers when you raise the request is still better where you can, because editing lines on an approved request sends it back to draft for approval again. Open the order to see its lines, then click PDF for the order document to send to the supplier. The platform does not email the order. Order statuses Status Meaning Open Nothing received yet. Partly received Some quantity has arrived. Received Everything has arrived. Cancelled Dropped, with a reason. Only an order with nothing received can be cancelled. Late (red badge) The expected date has passed and the delivery is not complete. Receive a delivery Open the order from the Orders tab (tick Only open orders to narrow it). In the Receive delivery block, set Received now for each line. It starts at what is still outstanding. Lower it for a part delivery. Set it to 0 to skip a line. For a stocked part, choose Into storeroom , or Direct use (not stocked) for something consumed straight away. If the part is lot- or serial-tracked, enter its lots or serial numbers. Type the Packing slip number from the delivery. Click Record receipt . Stock rises in the storeroom you chose and the receipt appears under Receipts with who received it and when. You cannot receive more than was ordered. Check the supplier's invoice (three-way match) When the invoice arrives, capture it from the order with Capture invoice (or from Payables). The invoice lines fill in from what was received and not yet invoiced. On the invoice, each line is marked Matches or Check : A line is flagged if the quantity invoiced so far is more than the quantity received. A line is flagged if the price is more than 2% above the order price. A line is flagged if it is not on the order at all (unless the invoice is for contractor work on a work order, which is checked against the work order's not-to-exceed amount instead). A person cannot approve an invoice they captured themselves. An invoice that does not match can still be approved, but the approver must type why it should be paid anyway. Details are on Payables . Suppliers and prices The Suppliers tab lists suppliers with their contact, payment terms, how many parts have prices and how many orders are open. Search by code or nam

title: Supplier requests for quote
text: When you need prices for something you buy, you can ask several suppliers at once. Create a quote request with the lines you need, choose the suppliers, record each supplier's answer as it comes in, compare them side by side and award each line. The award becomes a purchase request at the awarded prices. The platform does not send anything to suppliers. The request letter is a PDF you download and email yourself. When suppliers reply, you type their answers in. Nothing is sent or received automatically. Quote requests are part of the Standard edition, as part of Purchasing. The Lite edition has no purchasing. See quote requests : anyone who can view purchasing. Create, send, record replies, award, cancel : buyers (permission "manage purchasing"), for their own site. Create a quote request Open Sales & supply → Purchasing and click the Quote requests tab. Click New quote request . Choose the Site and give it a Title . Set Suppliers reply by (required before you can send) and, if useful, Goods needed by . Add Notes for the suppliers . Under Lines , pick a catalog part or choose Not a catalog part (describe it) . Enter the quantity and, if you have one, a Target price . Click Add a line for more. Under Suppliers to ask , tick each supplier you want to invite. At least one is needed to send. Click Save draft . Send it On the draft, click Request letter (PDF) and email it to each supplier yourself. Click Mark as sent . The request must have at least one supplier, a reply date and that date must not have passed. The status becomes Out for quotes . To drop a request, click Cancel on a draft or sent request and give a reason. Record the replies When a supplier answers, open the request. In the Suppliers table, click Enter their reply on their row. For each line, type the Unit price they quoted. Optionally add lead time in days, the minimum quantity and the date their price is valid until. Leave a line empty if they did not quote it. Enter Freight and Payment terms if they gave them. Click Save the reply . The supplier now shows Replied . If a supplier says no thanks, click They declined and say why if you know. You can fix a mistake later with Change reply while the request is out for quotes. Compare and award Once at least one supplier has replied, a Comparison table appears with one row per line and one column per supplier. The lowest price on each line is in bold and marked lowest . Under each price you see lead time, fastest where it is the quickest, the minimum quantity, and warnings: (below minimum) if your quantity is under their minimum and price expired if their valid-until date has passed. The bottom rows total Goods , Freight and Landed total per supplier, and show the Slowest line . best marks the lowest landed total. A supplier who did not quote every line is flagged not every line , so their total is not directly comparable. In the Award to column, choose the supplier for each line you want to place now. Leave others at Not yet . If you pick a supplier who is not the lowest price, a box asks Why not the lowest price? . Give a reason such as lead time, quality, minimums or a preferred supplier. It is required. Click Award the chosen lines . The page stays open and shows Awarded on PR-… draft with a Submit for approval button. Click it to send the purchase request through the normal approvals. The system creates a draft purchase request at the awarded prices. It stays a draft until you click Submit for approval (on the quote request, or on the request itself); the award itself does not approve spending, and nothing can be ordered before the request is approved. The button is for people who may raise purchase requests. See Purchasing . Awarded lines show Awarded and cannot be awarded again. When every line is awarded, the request status becomes Awarded and links to the purchase request. What the statuses mean Status Meaning Draft Being prepared. Not yet out. Out for quotes Marked as sent; waiting for replies. Replies late Out for quotes and the reply date has passed. Awarded Every line has been awarded and a purchase request created. Cancelled Dropped, with a reason. The list shows Replies as "2 of 4" so you can see who has answered. The buyer who made the request is reminded on the reply date and every day after while suppliers are still outstanding. Late requests also show on What is late , and the Supplier performance and other purchasing reports are in Reports . Common mistakes Expecting the platform to email suppliers. Download the letter and send it yourself. Comparing totals when a supplier skipped a line. Look for not every line before choosing the best total. Forgetting to submit the purchase request. The award leaves it as a draft; the Submit for approval button stays on the quote request until you use it. Who can run quote requests follows the "manage purchasing" permission on the role; see Roles and access . Purchase approval routes, by amount and spend type, are set by administrators; see Your first week .

title: Leasing
text: Leasing is for companies that rent out property. It shows every rental unit, who lives or works in it, what rent they pay, what they owe, and how long empty units stay empty. Open Sales & supply → Leasing . Leasing is part of the Standard edition. The Lite edition does not include it. See the rent roll and unit turns : property managers, finance approvers, billing clerks and executives (permission "view leasing"). Create and change leases, record notices and move-outs, add make-ready jobs, mark units ready, bill rent : property managers (permission "manage leasing"), for their own properties. The three tabs Pick a property in the box at the top right, or leave it on All my properties . Tabs: Rent roll , Unit turns and, if you can manage leasing, Rent billing . Rent roll The rent roll has one row per unit. The tiles above it show: Occupancy : occupied units (including those with notice given) out of rentable units. Units set offline are not counted. Rent + charges a month : monthly rent and recurring charges on occupied units. Vacant at market rent : what the empty units would bring in at their market rent. Past due : rent unpaid after the grace days. Unit status Meaning Occupied A lease is in force. Notice The renter has given notice. The move-out date is shown. Vacant Empty. The number of days vacant is shown, and any make-ready target date. Offline Not available to rent. Rows with money past due have a red edge. Click a row with a lease to open it. If there are no units, ask your administrator to import the unit directory, then rental units and leases (see Importing data ). Create a lease On a vacant unit with no lease waiting, click New lease . Enter the renter's name (required), email and phone. Set From and, unless the lease is month to month, To . Leave To empty for month to month. Check the monthly rent (it starts at the unit's market rent) and the deposit. Add one other monthly charge, such as parking, with an amount. Click Create draft lease . The lease opens as a draft. When the lease is signed, click Signed: start the lease . Only then does the lease take the unit. The renter becomes a customer in your customer list, so their invoices, payments and reminders live in Receivables . Lease status Meaning Draft Created, not yet signed. A draft can be cancelled. Active In force. The unit is occupied. Notice The renter has given notice to vacate. Ended Moved out. The unit goes into a turn. Renew, give notice, move out Open a lease. The Next step block shows the actions that fit its status. Renew : click Renew , set the New end date (empty for month to month) and the new rent, and click Renew . The new lease starts the day after the old one ends, with no turn in between. Notice to vacate : click Notice to vacate , enter the date notice was given and the date they are moving out, and click Record notice . The unit shows Notice in the rent roll. Move-out : click Record move-out , set the date they moved out (not in the future) and how many days you give yourself to make the unit ready ( Make ready within , 7 by default), and click Record move-out . The unit becomes vacant and a unit turn opens. Unit turns A turn is the make-ready period between one renter and the next. It opens when a move-out is recorded. The Unit turns tab shows the property and unit, when the renter moved out, the target ready date (with a red late badge if missed), days so far, jobs done out of jobs, Rent lost so far (market rent per day) and any lease already lined up. Click + job on a turn, describe the work (paint, clean, carpet, replace blinds) and click Add work order . Each job is a work order on the unit, which you can send to a contractor from the work order. See Work orders . When every job is done, click Mark ready . The button is disabled while jobs are still open. Tick Open turns only to hide finished turns. Bill the rent Open the Rent billing tab. The month defaults to the current month (or next month after the 20th). Read the preview: one row for each lease not yet billed for that month, with its lines and total. A prorated note marks an amount that was prorated. Click Issue N rent invoices to issue them, or Create as drafts to review them first in Receivables. Rent invoices are dated the 1st and due on receipt. Late means unpaid after the lease's grace days. Running the same month again only bills leases not yet billed. Payments, statements and reminders are handled in Receivables . The deposit is recorded as agreed; the accounting system holds the money. What is late Leases about to end and unit turns running late are in the daily reminders. The Rent roll and occupancy report in Reports gives the same data for export. Common mistakes Forgetting to click Signed: start the lease . A draft lease does not occupy the unit and is not billed. Recording a move-out without a make-ready target. The default of 7 days sets the late date; change it if the unit needs longer. Billing the wrong month. Check the Month field before you issue. Properties are sites of kind "property"; units, leases and renters are normally loaded with Data import. Rent invoices post through Receivables to your accounting connection or the built-in books. See Sites and people , Importing data and Accounting connection .

title: Books
text: The Books are a small-business set of accounts built into the platform. Customer invoices, supplier invoices, expense reports and payments post to them as they happen. You bring in your bank and card statements, match or categorize each line, reconcile to the statement, and read your profit and loss and balance sheet. Open Finance → Books . The built-in books are in both the Lite and Standard editions. They are an alternative to an external accounting system, not an addition to one: a company uses either the built-in books or a connected accounting system. They do not cover payroll processing, tax filing, multiple currencies, consolidation, fixed-asset depreciation schedules or inventory valuation. Read the overview, accounts, journal and statements : finance approvers, executives, bookkeepers and administrators (permission "view books"). Set up the books, categorize and match bank lines, add accounts, post journal entries, reconcile, close a period : bookkeepers and administrators (permission "manage books"). Set up the books The first time, if the books have not been set up, a Set up the books form appears. Only someone who can manage the books sees the form; others see a note that setup has not happened. Enter your main bank account's name (it starts as Checking ) and, if you like, its last four digits. Set Balance on to the date you want the books to start, and type the Opening balance the account had that day. Click Set up the books . This creates a starter chart of accounts, the bank account, and starts posting invoices, bills, expense reports and payments from then on. What customers still owe on invoices already issued, and what you owe on approved bills and expense reports, comes in as opening balances. Balances from a previous system come in from its trial balance (see below). If an external accounting connection is active, the setup page tells you to disconnect it under Accounting first. Only one accounting target is active at a time. See Accounting connection . The tabs Tab What it shows Overview Cash in the bank, what customers owe, what you owe suppliers, net income this month and this year, and warnings about bank lines to review or records that could not post. Banking Imported bank and card lines to match or categorize. The tab shows how many are waiting. Chart of accounts Your accounts with balances. Click one for its register. Journal Every entry this year, plus a form for manual entries. Statements Profit and loss, balance sheet and trial balance for a date range, and a journal export. Reconcile Agree the books to a bank statement. Settings Bring in open items, and close a period. Bank and card lines Bring in a statement Click Import a statement on the Banking tab. You go to Data import. Choose Bank and card transactions and upload your bank's CSV file. The importer reads the bank's own layout. See Importing data . Match or categorize each line Show Unreviewed lines (the default) and work down the list. For each line you have these choices: Match : if a payment you already recorded in the platform fits the amount and date, a button starting Match and the journal entry number appears. Click it to tie the bank line to that payment, so nothing is counted twice. Categorize : choose an Account (a rule may have suggested one) and click Categorize . Tick Rule first to remember it: later lines whose description contains the same words get the account suggested. Exclude : for lines that are not business transactions or are already recorded. Use the Show box to look at Matched , Categorized and Excluded lines later. The Rules table at the bottom lists the rules you have saved. Journal The journal records every posting as a balanced entry: total debits equal total credits. Entries are never edited; a correction is a reversal, shown with a Reversal or Reversed badge. The From column shows what created the entry: an invoice, bill, expense report, payment, bank line or a manual entry. Post a manual entry Use this for things that do not come from an invoice, bill, expense report or bank line: an owner contribution, a loan, a depreciation charge or a correction. On the Journal tab set the Date and a Memo saying what it is for. For each line choose an Account and enter a Debit or a Credit . Click Add line if you need more than two. Watch the line under the lines: it turns green when debits equal credits. Click Post entry . Chart of accounts The starter chart can be added to. Click Add an account at the bottom: give it a code, name and type (asset, liability, equity, income or expense). For an asset you can say whether it is a bank, current asset, fixed asset or inventory account. System accounts are marked (system) . Click any account in the list to see its register from the start of the year with opening and closing balances. Statements On the Statements tab choose a From and To date. You see the Profit and loss for the range, the Balance sheet as of the end date, and the Trial balance , which carries a Balanced or Out of balance badge. If the balance sheet does not balance, a red note says to check the journal. Click Export journal (CSV) to download every entry in the range. This is also the file to hand to a new accounting system if you move. Click Print or export the reports to open the Profit and loss report, where you can export Excel or PDF and print. See Reports . Reconcile to a statement Open the Reconcile tab. Choose the bank or card Account , set the Statement date and type the Ending balance from the statement. Click Start . Tick Cleared beside each deposit and payment that appears on the statement. Watch the three tiles: Statement balance , Cleared in the books and Difference . The difference turns green at zero. When the difference is zero, click Finish reconciliation . It moves to the Finished list. Only one reconciliation is open at a time. You cannot finish while the difference is not zero. Close a period Open Settings , find Close a period . Set Closed through to

title: Budgets
text: Budgets work in two directions at once. Bottom-up : each site and department builds its own lines by spend category. Top-down : finance sets targets, such as a company-wide ceiling, and compares them to the total. When the two agree, finance approves the budget, and from then on you can track actual spend against it. Open Finance → Budgets . Budgets are part of the Standard edition; the Lite edition does not include them. See spend history and budgets : maintenance, plant, quality, property, sales and HR managers, supervisors, buyers, executives, finance approvers (permission "view budgets"). Edit and submit lines : the head of a department can edit and submit that department's lines while the budget is a draft. Finance can edit all lines. Create budgets, set targets, review submissions, approve, close, manage spend categories : finance approvers (permission "manage budgets"). Spend history The first tab, Spend history , answers "where does the money go?". The headline says how much was spent in the last twelve months and which category took the largest share. Pick a site or leave All sites . The table has one row per spend category: a small bar for each month, the 12-month total, its share, the average per month, a Run rate (the last three months times four), and 2nd half vs 1st , which shows whether spending is rising or falling. The From column shows how much came from supplier invoices, stock used, expense reports and imported history. Below it, By site and department splits the total. History counts supplier invoices (not stock purchases), stock used, expense reports and any history your administrator imported. If a warning says some spend is on accounts no category includes, a finance approver should add those accounts to a category. Spend categories Finance sees a third tab, Spend categories . Each category collects spend from a list of accounts. An account belongs to only one category so nothing is counted twice. To change a category's accounts, click Edit beside it, change the comma-separated list and click Save . Create next year's budget On the Budgets tab, under New budget , enter the Fiscal year . The name is suggested, such as "2027 operating budget". Pick the month the year Starts in . Click Create . The budget opens as a draft. The list shows each budget's status, bottom-up total, company target and approval. Budget status Meaning Draft Being built. Lines, targets and reviews can change. Approved Finance approved it. It is now the plan to compare actual spend against. Closed Finance closed it, usually at the end of the year. Build the bottom-up lines Open the budget and stay on the Bottom-up lines tab. Lines are grouped by site and department. Each line has twelve monthly amounts, a year total and a basis that says how it was made. Start from history Under Start from history , choose a Site and, if you want, a Department (or leave Whole site (no department) ). Set Change % (it starts at 3) to raise or lower last year's pattern. Click Propose lines . The system adds a line for every category the site spent on in the last twelve months, keeping its monthly pattern. Add or adjust a line To add one by hand, use Add a line : choose site, department and category, enter the Year $ and choose Spread like history or Spread evenly . Click Add line . To change months, click Edit on the line, change the monthly numbers and click Save . Submit for review When a site or department is done, click Submit for review on its block. Submissions have their own status. Submission status Meaning Draft Not yet sent. Submitted Waiting for finance's review. Editing is locked unless you are finance. Accepted Finance is satisfied. Returned Finance sent it back with a note. Fix it and submit again. Top-down targets Finance uses the Top-down targets tab to compare the bottom-up total against a ceiling or goal. Choose what the target covers: a site, a department and a category, or leave any of them on All . A target with none selected covers everything. Enter the amount and an optional note such as "board ceiling". Click Set target . Read the table: Target , Bottom-up and the Gap (bottom-up minus target). A target is Within 2% when they are close, otherwise Bottom-up over or Bottom-up under . To close the gap by decree, click Allocate by bottom-up or by history . The target is spread over the lines it covers in proportion to those amounts, and they add up exactly. Reviews and approval On the Reviews tab, find submissions with status Submitted . Write a Note if needed, then click Accept or Return . When everything is ready, click Approve budget at the top of the budget. At the end of the year, click Close . The tiles at the top show the bottom-up total, the company target with the gap, the number of lines and the number of submissions waiting for review. Against actual The Against actual tab compares the plan with what has been spent. The headline says how much has been spent against the budget for the months elapsed, and a forecast for the year. The forecast is actual to date plus the budget for the months still to come. Committed counts open purchase orders for non-stock items. Status Meaning On track Spending and the forecast are within budget. Heading over The forecast for the year is more than 2% above the budget, or the recent run rate points that way. Over Actual spend plus committed orders is more than 5% above the budget to date. No budget Money is being spent in a category and site with no budget line. The Budget against actual report in Reports shows the same figures and can be exported. Common mistakes Editing after submitting. Once submitted, a department cannot edit unless finance returns it. Leaving accounts out of categories. Spend on an uncategorized account never reaches history or the budget comparison. Treating a target as a limit on spending. It only compares totals. It does not stop purchases. History can be filled with last year's spend through Data import → Spend histor

title: Business cases
text: A business case (also called a pro forma) is a spreadsheet-style model of an opportunity, kept inside the platform. You describe the revenue, costs and capital spending, and the system works out whether it is worth doing and when it pays for itself. You can try low, base and high scenarios, compare cases side by side, send the case for approval, and later check how the real results compare. Open Finance → Business cases . A business case is a model of your assumptions. It is not a forecast taken from your books. See business cases and compare them : finance approvers, operations (plant) managers, property managers, executives and district managers (permission "view business cases"). Create, edit, submit, copy and reopen : finance approvers, operations managers and property managers (permission "manage business cases"). Approve : the approver named at the top of the page. By default this is the owner (the administrators); an administrator can name someone else. Plan against actual : also needs permission to see the books. The list The page starts with a one-line summary of your cases. The Approved by line shows who approves cases. The table shows each case's number, title, kind, site, status, NPV , IRR , Payback , Funding needed and owner, all for the base case. Cases with a negative NPV have a red edge. NPV (net present value) What all the future cash is worth in today's money, after discounting at your discount rate. Positive means the case earns more than the rate; negative means it does not. IRR (internal rate of return) The yearly return the case earns on the cash put in. Shown as a dash if it cannot be worked out. Payback The number of months until cumulative cash turns positive. It reads No funding needed if cash never goes negative and Not within N years if it does not pay back in the period you modelled. Funding needed The lowest point cumulative cash reaches: the most you need to have available. Create a business case Click New business case . Enter a Title such as "Second store in Fort Worth". Choose the Kind : New site or store , New product or service , Customer contract , Capital project or Other opportunity . Choose a Site , or leave Company-wide (no site yet) . Set the First month and the number of Years (1 to 10). Under Start from choose Example drivers to replace (a starter set for that kind of opportunity), This site's last 12 months (only if you can see that site's books) or Nothing . Click Create . The new case opens. Edit the drivers Click Edit . The figures at the top update as you type; they use the same calculation as the saved result, and your work is kept on the server as you go, so a closed tab loses nothing. Lines are in four sections: Revenue Cost of sales Operating costs Capital spending Each line has a label and a way of calculating: Units × price , Amount per month , % of revenue , People × annual cost or One-time amount (which methods are offered depends on the section). You can also set growth per year, the month it starts and ends, a ramp-up in months for revenue, and the life in years for capital. The settings above the lines are the Discount rate % , Tax rate % and Working capital (days of revenue) . Scenarios The Scenarios table sets how the Low , Base and High cases differ: revenue %, costs %, capital % and a launch delay in months. Switch between them with the Low case , Base case and High case tabs. Everything on the page changes to show that scenario. Pull in numbers from elsewhere Above the lines, Pull in from adds lines drawn from the rest of the platform, which you then adjust: the site's books for the last 12 months, a budget, a CRM opportunity, a property's rent roll, an asset to replace, or the labor rate from work orders. Only sources you can see are offered. Click Save when finished, or Cancel to discard. Read the results The headline sentence gives the NPV and payback. The tiles show NPV, IRR, payback, funding needed, the First profitable month (the first month of positive operating profit before depreciation) and gross margin. Charts show cumulative cash and profit by year. A table gives profit and cash by year, and What moves the result pushes each driver down and up on its own and lists them by effect on NPV, largest first. This tells you which assumption to check hardest. The model uses straight-line depreciation, taxes profit after carrying losses forward, treats working capital as days of revenue (not released at the end) and discounts cash monthly. Compare cases On the list, tick Compare beside two or three cases. Click Compare N plans . Read the table of figures, the chart of cumulative cash and the table What differs , which lists only the assumptions that are not the same. You can also compare a case with one of its earlier revisions from Earlier revisions . Submit, approve, reopen When the case is ready, open it and click Submit for approval . The approver reviews it and approves or sends it back with a comment. Approval is a single step and a comment is required. The decision shows under Approvals . Approval freezes the lines and stores the approved base-case figures. To change a submitted or approved case, type a reason under Reopen and click Reopen . A submitted case is withdrawn from approval. An approved case starts a new revision that needs approval again, and the approved figures are kept so you can compare. Copy makes a new case from an existing one. Status Meaning Draft Being built or sent back. Editable. Submitted Waiting for the approver. Reopen to withdraw it. Approved Frozen. Its base case is the plan. Plan against actual Once a case for a site is approved and its start month has come, a Plan against actual block compares the plan with the site's posted books, month by month: revenue, operating profit and capital spent, with the months completed. It needs access to the books to appear. Its headline says whether the site is on track , behind or well behind. Common mistakes Leaving the example numbers in. The s

title: Receivables
text: Receivables is the money customers owe you. Open Finance → Receivables (the page heading reads Customer invoices ). Here you create and issue invoices, record payments, work the list of overdue customers and issue credit memos. In the Standard edition, invoices usually come from shipped sales orders. In Lite you type simple invoices directly. In both, issued invoices go to your accounting system or post to the built-in books, depending on your setup. See invoices, collections and customer accounts : billing clerks, finance approvers, bookkeepers, sales managers, property managers, executives (permission "view receivables"). Create, issue and void invoices, record payments, log collection calls, send reminders, issue credit memos : billing clerks, finance approvers, bookkeepers, property managers (permission "manage receivables"). Release an order from credit hold : finance approvers (permission "release credit holds"). The page Three tiles show Open receivables (balance on issued invoices), Overdue and Drafts . Tabs below them: Invoices , New invoice , Ready to invoice , Collections , Record payment and Credit memos . New invoice and Record payment only show if you can manage receivables. Ready to invoice is for Standard only. Status Meaning Draft Being prepared. No number yet. Not sent anywhere. Issued Numbered, dated and sent on to accounting or the books. Nothing paid yet. Part paid Some payment has been applied. Paid Fully paid. Void Cancelled, with a reason. Overdue (red badge) Issued or part paid and past its due date. Invoice what has shipped (Standard) Click the Ready to invoice tab. It lists orders with shipped quantity that has not been invoiced yet. Click Create invoice on an order. A draft invoice opens with the shipped lines. (You can also click Invoice what has shipped on the order itself.) Review the draft. See Issue the invoice below. Only one draft per order can exist at a time. To invoice part of what shipped now and the rest later, set a line's quantity to 0 on the draft. Type an invoice (no sales order) Click New invoice . Choose the Customer . Add Their PO (optional) . For each line enter a description, quantity, price and income type: Services , Products , Rent or Freight . Click Add line for more. Enter Sales tax $ if it applies. The total updates as you type. Click Create draft . Issue the invoice Open the draft. Click Preview PDF to see what the customer will get. To change it, click Edit draft . You can change freight, sales tax, the note on the invoice and each line's quantity. Save with Save draft . Click Issue invoice with the total on it. Issuing assigns the number, fixes the due date from the customer's terms, stores the PDF and sends the invoice to accounting on the next sync. After issuing you cannot edit the invoice. To correct it, void it (with a reason) and start again, or issue a credit memo. To throw away a draft, type a reason and click Discard draft . For an issued invoice the button reads Void invoice . Record a payment If your company's accounting system supplies payments, they arrive on each sync and you will see a note saying payments are not typed in. Otherwise: Click Record payment and choose the customer. Only customers with open invoices are listed. Enter Received on , the Amount , the Method (check, ACH, wire, card or other) and a check number or reference. The amount spreads over the customer's open invoices, oldest due date first. Change the Apply amounts to direct it elsewhere. Check the line Applied … of … . The two numbers must match. Click Record payment . You can also record a payment from an invoice or a customer's account page. Chase overdue accounts The Collections tab lists customers with overdue invoices, longest overdue first. It shows the contact and phone, the amount overdue, total open, how many days the oldest is overdue, the time of the last contact (a None badge if never) and any promise to pay. A promise date turns red when it passes. Accounts with an invoice more than 60 days overdue have a red edge. Call the customer. Click Log call on their row, write What was said , and set Promised to pay by (optional) . Click Save . On an open invoice you can also log a call against that invoice, or click Email payment reminder . The reminder goes to the customer's primary contact and is sent with the next mail run. You can send only one reminder per invoice per day. If the customer has no primary contact email, the button is disabled and says so. Overdue invoices also appear on What is late and trigger a weekly reminder summary to receivables staff at the site. Credit memos A credit memo reduces what a customer owes: a return, a price correction or goodwill. It is available only where payments are typed in (not when an accounting system issues credits). Open the issued or paid invoice and expand Credit this invoice . Or open the customer's account and use New credit memo . Enter the quantity to credit on each line. If goods come back, choose the returned part and the storeroom it goes into (not available in Lite); for lot- or serial-tracked parts, enter the lot or serial numbers. Add Sales tax credited and a Reason that shows on the memo. Click Draft credit memo , review it, then click Issue credit memo . Issuing numbers it, stores the PDF, returns goods to stock and applies it to the invoice it was raised against. Any credit left over is shown as Left to use . Use it from the memo page either to Apply it to another open invoice or to Record refund by check, ACH, wire, card or other. A memo that has been neither applied nor refunded can be voided with a reason. Customer account A customer's account page (open it from the invoice or the collections list) shows open invoices, ordered-but-not-invoiced orders, the Credit limit and Exposure . If exposure is over the limit, it is flagged and new orders from that customer go on credit hold. See Quotes and orders . Lite and Standard Lite has New invoice , payments, collections and c

title: Payables
text: Payables is where supplier invoices (called bills in the Lite edition) are entered, checked and approved for payment. Open it from Finance → Payables . The page heading reads Supplier invoices . What happens after approval depends on how your company does its accounting. With a connected accounting system, approved invoices are sent there and that system pays them. With the built-in books, approved invoices post to your books. Ask your administrator which applies to you. See supplier invoices : accounts payable clerks, bookkeepers, buyers, finance approvers, executives, district and property managers (permission "view payables"). Capture, approve, dispute, void and record payment : accounts payable clerks, finance approvers and bookkeepers (permission "manage payables"), for their own site. The invoice list Four tiles show Open payables , Overdue (the amount past its due date), Waiting for approval and Disputed . The table lists each invoice with supplier, number, site, purchase order, dates, amount and status. Overdue rows have a red edge and an Overdue badge. Untick Only unpaid to include paid and void invoices. Capture an invoice Click Capture invoice . (In Lite the button and page say Enter a bill .) Choose the Supplier . In Lite you can add a new supplier on the same page with a code and name. In Standard, choose the Purchase order if there is one. The lines fill in from what was received and not yet invoiced, with a note showing the order price, quantity received and quantity already invoiced. If there is no order, choose the Facility and add lines by hand with Add a line not on the order . Enter the Invoice number and Invoice date . Leave Due date empty to use the supplier's payment terms. Check each line's quantity, unit price and account. For lines from an order the account comes from the order; for others the default is Repairs & maintenance . Enter Freight and Sales tax if the invoice shows them, and attach the invoice file (PDF or image) under Invoice file . Check the Invoice total against the paper and click Save invoice . You can also start from a purchase order with Capture invoice on the order page. The match check On the invoice page every line shows Matches or Check . A banner Does not match the order lists the reasons. The system flags a line when: the quantity invoiced so far (across all invoices that are not void) is more than the quantity received; the unit price is more than 2% above the order price; the line is not on the purchase order (in Standard; in Lite a bill without an order is normal). Invoices for contractor work on a work order are also checked against the work order's not-to-exceed amount. See Purchasing for the order and receipt side. Approve for payment Open an invoice that is Waiting for approval (or Disputed ). If it matches, click Approve with the amount on the button. If it does not match, you must type Why should it be paid anyway? before the button is enabled. The note is kept on the invoice. You cannot approve an invoice you captured yourself. The page says so and someone else has to approve it. In a one-person company the licence may allow a sole owner to approve their own bill; the audit trail then records it as self-approved. Dispute or void Type a reason (at least three letters) in the box at the bottom. Dispute is for an invoice that is waiting for approval and needs the supplier to correct something; a disputed invoice can be approved later. Void cancels an invoice that should not be paid or was entered by mistake. Neither can be used on a paid or void invoice. Record payment Where your company does not pay through a connected accounting system, an approved invoice shows a Record payment block. Enter the date and the check or ACH reference and click Mark paid with the amount. The full invoice total is recorded. If an accounting system pays your bills, the payment comes back with its next sync and you cannot type it here. What the statuses mean Status Meaning Waiting for approval Captured; a second person must approve it. Approved Cleared for payment. Not yet in the accounting system. In accounting Delivered to the accounting system or posted to the built-in books. Paid Payment recorded or received back from accounting. Disputed Held while the supplier fixes something. Void Cancelled. It no longer counts toward what was invoiced against an order. The Accounting block on the invoice shows the sync: Create bill or Void bill , which connection received it, its status, the reference in the accounting system and any last error. A MOCK badge means a demonstration connection, not a real system. Invoices waiting for approval and overdue invoices are included in reminders, and overdue ones appear on What is late . The Accounts payable aging report in Reports shows how overdue they are. Lite and Standard Lite : bills are entered line by line, with no purchase order. The match check does not treat a missing order as a problem. Approved bills post to the built-in books. Standard : invoices are matched to purchase orders and receipts, and approved invoices go to the connected accounting system or the built-in books. Common mistakes Entering the same invoice twice. Search the list first; two entries double the quantity invoiced against the order and trip the match check. Typing freight or tax into a line. Use the Freight and Sales tax fields so they post to the right accounts. Approving a mismatch without understanding it. The note is the only record of why it was paid. Approved invoices follow the accounting connection set under Accounting. With no connection, or a file-export connection, payments are typed in here. See Accounting connection and Books .

title: Reports
text: Reports turn your records into answers. Each report opens with a headline sentence that states its main finding, then shows the key numbers, a few supporting points, charts and the full table behind them. The same figures appear on screen and in every export, for the same filters. Open Insight → Reports . Open reports : most roles have the right to run reports (permission "view reports"). Each report also needs the right to see the underlying records. For example, the Accounts payable aging report needs the right to view payables, and a business case report needs the right to view business cases. If you open one you lack the right for, the system tells you. Export to CSV, Excel and PDF, and share a saved view : managers, buyers, finance and sales staff, bookkeepers and executives (permission "export reports"). The export buttons do not appear for people without it. Delete a saved view : its owner, or an administrator. Choose a report The Reports page lists the reports available to your company as cards with a one-line description. Click one to run it. The list is shorter if your edition or switched-off features exclude some. In the Lite edition you get Profit and loss , Balance sheet , Accounts receivable aging , Accounts payable aging and the expense summary. Reports most relevant to the sales and finance pages are: Report What it answers Accounts receivable aging What customers owe by how overdue, promises to pay, shipments not invoiced, orders on credit hold. See Receivables . Accounts payable aging Unpaid supplier invoices by how overdue, due this week, waiting for approval. See Payables . Profit and loss, Balance sheet Statements from the built-in books. See Books . Budget against actual Spend against the approved budget with a forecast. See Budgets . Business cases The portfolio of business cases. See Business cases . Rent roll and occupancy Units, rent, occupancy and balances. See Leasing . Sales pipeline Open opportunities by stage, quotes awaiting a decision, win rate, orders booked and late. Quote aging, Quote outcomes Quotes waiting by age and expiry; sent quotes by outcome, with decline reasons and how often validity was extended. See Quotes and orders . Customer quote requests Days to send a quote, share answered on time, bid decisions and win rate by source. See Customer requests for quote . Purchasing status, Purchase order aging, Supplier performance Requests, open and late orders, committed spend and supplier delivery. See Purchasing . Payment behavior How late each customer pays and how late you pay each supplier over twelve months. Read a report The headline. The large sentence at the top is the report's finding, such as "Net income $42,000 on $310,000 of income (13.5% margin)" or "No open customer invoices in scope". Read it first; the rest supports it. The line under it shows the period (if the report has one), the scope (which sites the numbers cover) and when it was generated, in UTC. The tiles are the key numbers. A tile's color shows its status: green is good, amber needs a look, red is bad, no color is neutral. A small note gives context such as a target. The supporting points list three to five facts behind the headline. The charts show the same numbers visually. If your personal setting prefers tables, charts are folded into a Charts section you can open. The table has every row. Rows with a red edge need attention. A dash means no data is available, which is not the same as zero. The notes under the table explain definitions and data limits, and name the source. When a row links to a source record, an Open link at its right takes you to it. Tables with eight or more rows have a search box and sorting for the rows already loaded. Filter a report In Filters and saved views , set the filters the report offers. They differ by report; common ones are Site (default All my sites ), From , To , As of , Days back and Fiscal year . Click Apply . The page and the address both change, so you can bookmark or share the link. Click Reset to go back to the defaults. You only ever see data for the sites you are allowed to see. Two people running the same report can get different numbers because their scope differs. Save a view Set the filters you use often and click Apply . Under Name these filters , type a name (at least two letters). Tick Share with the company if you want others to use it. This tickbox appears only for people who can export reports. Click Save view . Choose a view from Saved views to apply it. Saving under an existing name of your own replaces it. Delete view appears next to the view you have selected if it is yours (or you are an administrator). Export and print If you can export, three buttons sit at the top right of the report. Button What you get CSV A plain table that opens in any spreadsheet. It begins with a few lines describing the report, finding, period, scope and filters, so a forwarded file explains itself. Percentages are written as ratios from 0 to 1. Blank cells mean no data, not zero. Excel A workbook with the same figures. PDF A formatted document with the tiles, charts and table. Use this to print or send by email. Each export uses the filters currently applied and is recorded in the audit trail with the filters and the number of rows. To print, download the PDF and print that. Reports and "what is late" Reports describe a period or a point in time and can be exported. What is late is a live list of items already past their date. Use it for daily follow-up and reports for analysis. Common mistakes Reading a dash as zero. A dash means the figure could not be worked out from the data. Comparing two people's numbers. Check the scope line; different sites give different totals. Forgetting the period. Check From and To before you export for someone else. Which reports appear follows the edition and the feature switches; the role that lets someone export reports is set in role settings. See Features and editions and Permissions table .

title: What is late
text: "What is late" collects every date that has passed, across the whole platform, on a single page: money owed to you and by you, quotes and orders, work and maintenance, calibration and reviews. Use it as your morning check. Open Insight → What is late . It is in the menu for everyone. Who sees what: each section appears only if you are allowed to see that kind of record, and only for the sites you can see. A bookkeeper sees invoices and bills; a technician sees work orders and preventive maintenance. Nobody sees a section they have no access to. If nothing at all is late for you, the page says "Nothing you can see is past its date." How to read the page Read the sentence at the top. It gives the total number of late items and the four biggest groups, such as "14 items are past their date: 6 customer invoices past due; 4 work orders past their due date; …". Look at the tiles. They show up to five groups with the count and, where there is money, the total amount. Scroll to the section you care about. Each shows a count and an amount in its heading. Rows show the item, what is wrong, the owner, Days late and the amount. Click the item name to go to its record and fix it. Each section shows the 40 most overdue items. If there are more, a note says "Showing the 40 most overdue of N". Fix the oldest and the list refills. Group by owner Tick Group by owner to flip the page. Instead of one section per kind of item, you get one block per person, biggest pile first, so a manager can see who has the most overdue. Items with no known owner appear under No owner recorded .
