The owner is the person who prepared or is responsible for the item, or for an invoice, the customer's account owner. What counts as late Section Counts when Needs access to Customer invoices past due Issued or part-paid and unpaid after the due date. Amount is the balance still owed. Receivables Supplier bills past due Waiting for approval, approved, in accounting or disputed, and past the due date. It says which: not yet approved, disputed or approved and unpaid. Payables Purchase orders past the promised date Open or part-received, with quantity still to come, after the expected date. Amount is the value still to arrive. Purchasing Quote requests still waiting for replies Supplier quote requests out for quotes, past the reply-by date, with at least one supplier not yet answered. It names who we are waiting for. Purchasing Quotes expired without a decision Sent quotes past their valid-until date with no acceptance or decline. Sales Customer requests for quote past their reply date Requests still needing a decision or being bid, after the reply-due date. Sales Sales orders late to ship Open or part-shipped orders after the promised ship date. Sales Work orders past their due date Not yet completed, verified, closed or cancelled and past due. The owner is the assigned people. Work orders Preventive maintenance overdue Active PM plans past their next-due date. Work orders Change notices waiting for acknowledgement Issued notices where someone required to acknowledge has not, after the acknowledge-by date. Changes Temporary procedure changes past their end date Still in force after the end date. Changes Service visits past their due date Planned, scheduled, dispatched or in progress after the due date. Notes unassigned visits. Field service Production orders past their due date Planned, released or in progress after the due date. Production Calibrations overdue Active calibration plans past the next-due date. Quality Specification reviews overdue Customer specification revisions waiting for their impact review past the due date. Documents Readings not acknowledged Documents people were required to read and have not, past the due date. Shows how many people. Documents "Days late" counts calendar days from the due date to today. What to do with it Customer invoices : open Receivables , go to Collections and call. Supplier bills : approve or dispute them in Payables . Purchase orders and quote requests : chase the supplier from Purchasing or Supplier requests for quote . Quotes : extend, revise or record the outcome. See Quotes and orders . Customer requests : decide to bid or not, or quote. See Customer requests for quote . Work, maintenance, calibration : see Work orders , Preventive maintenance and Quality . Things to know The page is live: it shows today's status each time you open it. It is not a saved report. For a dated snapshot you can export, use Reports . Some links go to the list page for that area rather than the exact record, because several items share one list. In the Lite edition, sections for areas Lite does not include (such as purchasing, quotes, work and production) have nothing to show. You also get reminders by notification for many of these items. See Notifications and reminders . Late dates come from each record. Reminder timing and who receives which reminder are set under Reminders. See Reminders and retention .

title: Your first week
text: This page is the short route from a freshly installed system to a company that is ready to use. It is written for the person who will administer the system: you do not need to be a developer, but you should be comfortable with spreadsheets, your company's sign-in service, and working with whoever hosts the server. Each day lists what to do and where to read more. Smaller companies can fold several days into one. Everything under the Admin menu heading needs the administrator role (the tenant.admin permission). The first administrator is created when the company is set up on the server (see First deployment ); that person does the steps below. Before day one: the server Whoever runs the server does this once. It is not an Administrator-screen task, but nothing else works until it is done. The server is installed with its two database logins, a persistent folder for uploaded files, and a secure (https) address. /ready answers OK. The company and its first administrator exist, and you have been given a sign-in token for that administrator (a long code beginning erp_ ). Someone has decided who will send email (see Scheduled jobs : the digest email is not delivered until a mail service is connected) and where backups go. Details are in Security and operations . Day 1: sign in, then describe the company Open the address. On the Sign in page, open the fold-out Development sign-in with an API token , paste the administrator token and choose Sign in with token . (Single sign-on comes on day 3.) Open Admin → Fit interview and answer the questions about what the business does. Choose Save answers and show the recommendation . You get a suggested set of features, a suggested plan depth and a list of things that are not a fit yet. Read the fit interview before pressing the optional Hide the features we did not recommend button; you can leave it for day 4. Open Admin → Implementation . Pick a depth ( Guided , Standard or Full ), optionally a target go-live date, and choose Build the plan . The plan is your checklist from here on. See Implementation planner . Open Admin → Sites and add every plant, store, warehouse, office or property. Give each its right time zone. See Sites . Many sites at once: use the Sites (properties, stores, plants) import. Day 2: people and roles Open Admin → Data import and load Employees / technicians from your payroll or HR export (no pay data needed). See Importing data . Add the people who sign in. One at a time: Admin → People and access , Add a person , then Give role with the site (or All sites ). Many at once: load People who sign in, with roles in the import, one row per person and role, with the work email, the employee number, the role and the site (blank means all sites). See People who sign in . If a starter role does not fit, make a company role on the Roles tab (Standard). Give at least two people the Administrator role. A company rollback needs a second administrator to confirm it (see Archives and recovery ), and you do not want one lost login to lock everyone out of administration. In Admin → Implementation , mark the steps Verify as you check them and give each remaining step an Owner . Day 3: single sign-on Ask whoever runs your identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta and similar) to register the platform as a web application, using the redirect address shown on Admin → Sign-in . Enter the issuer, client id, client secret and your work-email domains. Tick Single sign-on is on and save. Sign out, and sign back in with your work email. Ask a second person to try. Once two people have signed in this way, revoke the first administrator token under Admin → People and access → Tokens (it expires by itself after 14 days), and decide whether to switch off API tokens. Issue any tokens your scripts need there, each with an expiry. All the details, including what to give the provider, are in Sign-in . Day 4: tailor what people see and what reminds them Admin → Features : hide the areas the company does not use, or show some of them to only some roles. See Features and editions . Admin → Reminders : look through the 33 reminders the system sends, turn off the ones you do not want and adjust lead times. See Reminders and retention . Admin → Data retention : confirm how long short-lived working data is kept. The defaults are sensible for most companies. If the company uses the built-in books, set them up in Books ; if it uses outside accounting software, open Admin → Accounting . See Accounting connection . Day 5: rehearse, protect, and check the machinery In the Rehearse and go live section of the plan, make a practice copy and run your real files through it before loading the real company. See Practice copy . Load the rest of the data steps in the order the plan gives. Each import has a check step that saves nothing; fix the problems file and try again. See Importing data . Open Admin → Archives and restore and choose Archive now , so you have a clean starting point. Ask the server operator to confirm that database backups are running and that a restore has been tried ( backup drill ). Open Admin → Scheduled jobs and choose Run it now for this company once to see that every step reports done. See Scheduled jobs . Complete Final changes and cutover and Go-live sign-off in the plan. After go-live: the routine How often What Every day (automatic) The daily job runs: reminders, email digests, retention, archives and document reviews. Glance at Scheduled jobs now and then. Weekly Check that Scheduled jobs shows a recent day; look at Admin → Accounting for items that Need attention if you use a connection. Quarterly Review who has the Administrator role and who has left ( People and access : disable leavers, check Last used on tokens and revoke any that are not needed); ask the server operator to run the backup drill; review the Features and Reminders settings. title: Sites and people
text: Three things decide what a person sees in the system: which sites exist, which roles the person has, and where each role was granted. This page covers all three. Nothing here is created by signing in: a person must be added by an administrator first. Adding or changing sites, groups, people and role grants needs the administrator role (the People and access screen is shown only to administrators). A maintenance manager can open Sites (menu Admin → Sites ) to see the sites and create request links for the sites they manage, but cannot add or edit a site. Sites A site is a plant, store, warehouse, office, property or anything else with its own address and people. Nearly everything in the system hangs off a site: work orders, stock, timesheets, approvals. Add a site Open Admin → Sites and choose Add site . Fill in Code (up to 30 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or digit; it must be unique), Name , the kind, and the Time zone (a name such as America/Chicago ; the default is America/New_York , so change it if the site is elsewhere). Timestamps in imports without a time zone are read in the site's time zone. Optionally fill in Street , City , State and ZIP . Choose Save . To retire a site, choose Edit on its row and clear Active . Sites are never deleted. The kinds are Property, Store, Plant, Warehouse, Office and Other. For many sites at once, use Admin → Data import and choose Sites (properties, stores, plants) ; a portfolio, region or district column creates the group and adds the site to it. See Importing data . Limits that come with the licence Properties: a plan covers up to 100 active properties (it may be lower for a smaller plan). Adding or reactivating a property beyond it fails with “your plan covers up to N properties and N are active; deactivate a property you no longer manage to add another”. The summary tile Properties licensed shows use against the limit. Stores: a plan covers up to 5 active stores, enforced the same way, with a similar message and a Stores licensed tile. Plants, warehouses, offices and other kinds are not counted. Lite edition: one site and five active users in all. See Features and editions . Field service is licensed per site. A new site starts with the standard modules (core, assets, maintenance, documents, imports and reporting). Field service is switched on for a site by whoever operates your licence (there is no customer screen for it; see Features and editions ). Groups A group is a named set of sites: a portfolio, region, district or other. Its use is access: a role granted on a group covers every site in it, now and later. At the bottom of Admin → Sites , choose Add group . Give it a Code , a Name and a kind (Portfolio, Region, District or Other), tick the sites in it, and choose Save group . Adding a site to a group later gives everyone with a role on that group the new site (the screen says: at their next sign-in). Request links A request link lets someone without a login (a resident, a store employee) report a problem at one site. On a site's row choose Request links , type a label such as “Residents, lobby poster”, and choose Create link . Copy the link at once : it is shown only once. Requests arrive under Work orders → Requests . Choose Revoke to switch a link off. The public page asks for the place, a description, a name and contact, and (for properties) permission to enter. Public pages are rate limited by address; see Rate limits . People who sign in A person who signs in is a user . An employee is a record in the directory (name, job title, site, manager). The two are linked by employee number, but they are separate: you can have employees who never sign in, and users who are not employees (an outside accountant, for example). Add one person Open Admin → People and access (the Users tab) and choose Add a person . Type the person's Full name and Work email , then choose Add person . The email is kept in lower case and must not already belong to a user of your company. The person's row opens. Choose a role and where it applies in Give role (see Roles and where they apply ). Until you do, the person can sign in but sees almost nothing, and the page says No role yet . The licence's user limit applies here too: in Lite the sixth active user is refused with “licence: 5 of 5 users are active, the most the lite edition includes; disable a user or upgrade”. Add many people: the import To add people in bulk, use the import. Load the sites and the employees first (the implementation plan enforces this order). Open Admin → Data import , choose People who sign in, with roles and download the Excel or CSV template. Fill in one row per person and role : Work email (required), Name (required for a new person), Employee number (links to the employee record; a warning, not an error, if it is not found), Role (required; the role's name, such as Maintenance Manager ) and Site code . Repeat the person on a second row for a second role. Leave Site code blank to grant the role at all sites . A role granted at a site works only at that site. Upload, match columns, check every row, and import. Committing this target needs the administrator role. Things to know: Emails are matched in lower case. Running the import again for an existing email updates the name and adds any new role; a role the person already has is skipped quietly. The licence's user limit applies. When it is reached the database refuses with a message that starts “licence: N of N users are active”. An unknown role name is an error on that row; the message lists some valid names. The first time a person signs in with single sign-on, the system links them by their verified email. See Sign-in . Roles and where they apply Open a person with Manage on their row in Admin → People and access . Under Roles you see every role they hold and where it applies: all sites, one site, or a portfolio (a group of sites). To gi

title: Sign-in and access tokens
text: People sign in through the company's own identity provider using OpenID Connect (OIDC), the standard behind “Sign in with Microsoft” and “Sign in with Google”. It works with Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Auth0, Keycloak and any provider that publishes a discovery document. The platform keeps no passwords. The other way in is an API token , meant for scripts and for the first administrator before single sign-on is set up. Only an administrator sees Admin → Sign-in . Setting it up usually needs a second person who administers the identity provider. What to give the identity provider Ask the provider's administrator to register a new web application (a “confidential client”) with these settings. Setting Value Redirect URI (sign-in redirect URL, reply URL) Shown on the page as Redirect URL . It is your public address followed by /auth/sso/callback , for example https://erp.example.com/auth/sso/callback . It comes from the server's APP_BASE_URL setting, so check it is right before you hand it over. Flow Authorization code, with PKCE (the system always sends a PKCE challenge). Scopes openid email profile Client authentication A client secret, sent to the provider with HTTP Basic authentication. A client with no secret also works (the secret field may stay empty). ID token signature RS256 or ES256 . Tokens signed any other way are refused. In return you need three things: the issuer address (for Microsoft Entra ID it looks like https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0 ), the client id , and the client secret . Claims the system reads Claim Used for sub The person's permanent identity at the provider. Required. After the first sign-in the account is tied to the pair (issuer, sub ). email Finding the user on the first sign-in. email_verified Must be true for the first sign-in to link by email. Some providers do not send it unless you ask for it as an optional claim; if people see “the provider did not confirm the email address”, this is the cause. iss , aud , exp , iat , nonce Checked for you: the issuer must match, the token must be for this client id, must not be expired (one minute of clock drift is allowed) and must belong to this sign-in attempt. The name claim is not used; names come from your people import. Set it up Open Admin → Sign-in (the page title is Sign-in ). Copy the Redirect URL to the provider's administrator and wait for the issuer, client id and secret. Enter the Issuer (it must start with https:// ; a trailing slash is removed), Client id and Client secret . In Work-email domains enter the domains your staff use, separated by commas, for example example.com, example.co.uk . Leave Link a person's first sign-in by their verified email ticked (see below). Tick Single sign-on is on and choose Save . When it is on, the system fetches the provider's discovery document to check it can be reached. If it cannot, you get an error and nothing is turned on. Sign out and sign in as a person: on the Sign in page type your work email and choose Continue with your company account . The secret is write-only. After saving, the field shows “Saved (leave blank to keep)”. It is stored encrypted with the server's SSO_SECRET_KEY ; if that key is lost, you must enter the secret again. To rehearse before you have a real provider, the server operator can run a test provider with npm run mock-idp . It is only for trials. How people are matched to accounts Finding the company. The person types an email. The system looks at the part after the @ and finds the company whose Work-email domains contain it. A domain can belong to only one company; saving a domain another company already uses fails. (A direct link can also name the company.) Signing in at the provider. The person is sent to the provider, signs in there, and comes back. Finding the user. If the identity (issuer and sub ) is already linked to an active user, that user is signed in. Otherwise, if the email is verified and the option is ticked, the system looks for an active user with that email that has never been linked , links it, and signs in. Otherwise the person sees “<email> is not a user of <company>; ask your administrator to add you”. Things the rules imply: Nobody is created by signing in. Add people first, one at a time under Admin → People and access or in bulk with the People who sign in, with roles import ( Sites and people ). The domain list only decides which company to send the person to. It does not restrict who may sign in. What decides access is an active user with a matching verified email, or an already linked identity. If you untick Link a person's first sign-in… , nobody who is not already linked can sign in for the first time. Leave it ticked unless you have a specific reason. Each user can be linked to one identity only. If you change to a different issuer, people linked to the old one cannot be matched again by email while they are still linked. Before changing provider , open each person under Admin → People and access and choose Unlink (see Single sign-on identity ), then change the provider here. At their next sign-in they are matched by verified email and linked to the new identity, provided Link a person's first sign-in… is ticked. If the new provider reports a different email, add the identity by hand with Link identity . Single sign-on gives a session that lasts 12 hours . Signing out ends it at once. API tokens An API token is a long code beginning erp_ that stands in for a password. It lets a script, or a person at the development sign-in fold-out, act as one user with that user's roles. Only a fingerprint of the token is stored, so a lost token cannot be shown again. Administrators issue and revoke tokens under Admin → People and access → Tokens (see below). title: Features and editions
text: Two separate controls decide which parts of the system a person can use. Features are yours: you choose, area by area, who sees it. Editions and licences are the commercial limits that come with the plan the company bought: the edition (Lite or Standard), caps on properties and stores, and whether field service is licensed for a site. Both apply at once: a feature has to be allowed by the licence and shown to the person. Only an administrator sees Admin → Features . Editions and licences are not changed on any screen; the platform operator changes them (see Licences ). The Features page Open Admin → Features . It lists all 33 features in seven groups (My day, Company, Maintenance, Production, Quality & safety, Sales & supply, Finance). At the top it tells you how many are limited or turned off. Each feature has a selector with three choices: Choice What happens Everyone (the default) Everyone whose roles allow it sees the feature. Only some roles You tick the roles that see it (each shows how many people hold it). People without a ticked role do not see it. Nobody (hidden) Nobody sees it. It remains on this page so you can bring it back. Change a feature Find the feature and change its selector. If you chose Only some roles , tick at least one role (the Save button stays off until you do). Read the yellow note if one appears. It says what else is affected (for example, hiding Purchasing means planning and reorder suggestions create purchase requests nobody will see). Choose Save . The row shows when it was changed and by whom. The setting applies at once for new page loads (it is cached for at most 30 seconds). What “hidden” does The feature's permissions are taken away from the roles it is hidden from, so every existing check hides or refuses it. Its menu entries disappear, and the system refuses its pages, data and reports for someone who can see it nowhere. They get “<Feature> is turned off for your role. An administrator can turn it on under Admin → Features.” (error feature_off , status 403). Records are not deleted and nothing is lost. Turn the feature back on and everything is as it was. People are not asked to approve records of a feature they cannot see (expenses, purchase requests, quotes, changes, temporary changes, FMEA, continuity plans and business cases). A reminder belonging to a feature that is off for everyone is not sent. The Reminders page says so. The administrator is treated like everyone else: if you restrict a feature to some roles and leave out Administrator , you will not see it either, though you can still change the setting here. Home, approvals, notifications, reports and the administration screens are always available and are not features. Features that lean on each other Assets hidden: only the register pages go; work orders, PM and production still use assets. Work orders hidden: PM and the shift log rely on them. Storerooms and lots hidden: receiving into stock, kits and production issues need them. Production hidden: planning works from production routings. Quality hidden: FMEA and SPC live on the Quality page. Time and timesheets hidden: safety incident rates use timesheet hours. Training and qualifications hidden: qualification checks on work orders and machines still apply, but nobody can grant new qualifications. Customers and Purchasing hidden: invoices and bills still choose customers and suppliers; only their own pages go. Books hidden: postings continue while the built-in books are the accounting connection. Let the fit interview suggest settings The fit interview ( Admin → Fit interview ) recommends features from answers about the business. Its button Hide the features we did not recommend sets those features to Nobody (hidden) in one go. It is reversible here. See Implementation planner . Lite and Standard The edition is part of the licence and applies to the whole company. Both editions use the same records, so moving from one to the other migrates nothing. Lite Standard Sites 1 As licensed (properties up to 100, stores up to 5) Active users 5 As licensed News, people directory, handbook and policies, search Yes Yes Expense reports Yes; the owner approves Yes; routed by department, site and amount Customers, simple invoices, payments, collections Yes Yes, plus quotes, sales orders and shipments Suppliers and bills Yes (bills without purchase orders) Yes, plus purchasing and three-way checks Built-in books Yes Yes, or an external accounting system Data import (bank statements, customers, suppliers, history) Yes Yes Reports Profit and loss, balance sheet, receivables aging, payables aging, expense summary All Assets, maintenance, PM, storerooms, production, quality, safety, planning, budgets, leasing, store operations, field service Not included Yes (subject to the feature settings and licences) In Lite, anything outside its areas answers with: “This is part of the Standard edition. Your company uses Lite (books, invoicing, bills, expenses, policies and the intranet); an administrator can upgrade.” (error edition , status 403). Lite lets one person approve their own expense report, bill or reimbursement when they are the only person who could sign. The audit trail records it as self-approved. The moment someone else could sign, the normal rule applies again. Prices are commercial matters and are not in the software; the software only enforces what each edition includes. Not in any edition: payroll processing, tax filing, multi-currency, consolidation, fixed-asset depreciation schedules and inventory valuation in the books. Moving from Lite to Standard The platform operator changes the edition. Then keep the built-in books (Standard modules post through them the same way), or move to an external accounting system: export the journal, import opening balances into the new system, disconnect the books under Admin → Accounting and connect the new one. title: Reminders and retention
text: Two pages under Admin shape the system's daily housekeeping. Reminders decide what the system nags people about, how early, and how often. Data retention decides how long throw-away working data (read notifications, old import rows, sent emails and similar) is kept. Both are applied by the daily job ( Scheduled jobs ), so changes take effect from the next daily run. Reminders is open to administrators, and also to anyone an administrator has allowed to change a particular reminder (by default, the managers of that area). Data retention is for administrators only. Email delivery. Reminders always arrive in the notification bell. The daily email digest is built and queued, and it is sent when the server has a mail server set up ( SMTP_HOST , see Configuration ); without one the server only writes the messages as files under its storage folder ( mail ) and sends nothing. The sending code has been verified only against a stand-in mail server in the test suite, not against a real provider (an owner decision, see What is not done ), so until you have used Send a test email to me on the Scheduled jobs page and seen it arrive, tell people to rely on the bell. The plan step Outgoing email tracks this. Reminders Open Admin → Reminders . The page lists all 33 reminders in groups (Maintenance, Quality, Safety, People, Purchasing and finance, Stock and sites). The line at the top says how many exist and how many are turned off. For each reminder you see what triggers it, who receives it, and whether it is on. Change a reminder Find the reminder, for example Calibration due soon . Tick or untick Send this reminder . If it has a lead time, set the number of days. The wording follows the reminder: Warn N days ahead ; After N days overdue ; Every N days ; or Flag nothing measured in N days . The allowed range and the default appear under the row; a number outside the range cannot be saved. Choose how often it repeats: Every day , Once a week or Once only . Each reminder allows only some of these. Choose Save . The row records who changed it and when. What the reminders cover Group Examples Maintenance PM plans due without a work order; overdue work orders; kits short of parts; missed condition readings; equipment warranties expiring Quality SPC alarm summary; calibration due soon and overdue; overdue actions; effectiveness checks due; unanswered supplier corrective action requests; audits coming up Safety Incidents not yet classified; temporary changes ending; continuity plan reviews and exercises People Training due; qualifications and external certificates expiring; performance reviews due and well overdue; timesheets not submitted and waiting for approval Purchasing and finance Late purchase orders; contractor insurance expiring; supplier invoices waiting; overdue customer invoices; accounting sync problems; next year's budget not started; follow-up tasks due; quotes about to expire Stock and sites Lots expiring; store walks not done; leases ending and unit turns late Rules to know A reminder whose feature is turned off for everyone ( Features ) is not sent; the row shows a note saying so. Recipients are fixed by the reminder (for example “the assigned technicians” or “quality staff at the site”). You choose whether and how early, not who. Each person can also mute kinds of notification for themselves ( Notifications and reminders ). Items marked New are reminders for which nothing existed before; look through them when you first open the page. Who may change a reminder Administrators see a selector under each reminder: Changed by administrators and managers of the area (the default: whoever holds the area's manage permission, for example quality.manage for calibration) or Changed by administrators and chosen roles , where you tick the roles. Choose Save who may change it . People who may change only some reminders see only those on this page, and the menu entry appears for them. Periodic reviews At the top of the Reminders page is a block titled Periodic reviews for records that must be re-confirmed regularly: FMEAs, SPC characteristics and limits, controlled documents, policies and handbook, the expense policy, training course content, user access, approved suppliers, PM plans, critical spares lists, repair templates, store walk checklists and business continuity plans. For each you set whether reviews are tracked, how many months between them, how many days ahead to warn, the repeat, and how many days overdue before managers (or administrators) are told too. Defaults are in the 6 to 24 month range; the page shows the limits. The User access review reminds administrators every six months by default to look at who holds which role; it is a good habit. Data retention Open Admin → Data retention . The daily job deletes only short-lived working data, after a period you can adjust. The sentence at the top says how many items the next sweep will remove. Category Default Allowed What it is Rows of finished imports 90 days 7 to 3650 The staged rows of an import, which hold the values from the uploaded file. The summary (file name, mapping, counts) stays. Imports checked but never run are cancelled after the same period. Read notifications 180 days 30 to 3650 Counted from when the person read them. Unread notifications 365 days 90 to 3650 The records they point to are not affected. Sent emails 90 days 7 to 3650 Copies of digests and reminders that were sent or failed. Emails still waiting are never removed. Unsaved form entries 90 days 7 to 3650 What people typed into a form and never saved or discarded, counted from the last change. Expired sign-in tokens 30 days 1 to 3650 Tokens past their expiry or revoked. Unfinished single sign-on attempts go after a day. One more period is fixed and cannot be changed: saved replies for retried requests, kept 7 days (they let a phone that lost its connection resend a change without doing it twice). title: Importing data
text: The import wizard loads data from the files a company already has (CSV, Excel or JSON) without custom programming. It matches your columns to the system's fields, checks every row before anything is saved, tells you exactly what is wrong with the rows that fail, and can remember the mapping for next time. Importing the same file again updates records instead of duplicating them. Anyone with the imports.run permission can open Admin → Data import and check a file. Saving the rows needs imports.commit and , for most targets, the permission of the area being loaded (for example books.manage for bank lines, purchasing.manage for suppliers, tenant.admin for sites and people). Finance, buyers, sales and production roles hold the right pairs for their own data; see the Permissions table . Run an import Open Admin → Data import . The page is called Bring in existing data and shows four stages: Choose file , Match columns , Check , Imported . Under What are you importing? pick a target (the table below). A short description appears. No file yet? Choose Excel template or CSV template : you get a file with the column names the importer recognises, an example row and an explanation of every column. In Where does the file come from? type a short name for the source system, such as old-cmms or payroll . Use the same name every time you load from that system; it is how a later load finds the same records. If every row belongs to one site, choose it under Default facility ; otherwise leave it and let the rows name their sites. Choose the file ( .csv , .tsv , .xlsx or .json ; an old .xls must be saved as .xlsx or CSV first). Uploads are limited to about 50 MB by default. Choose Match columns . On Match columns , each system field shows the column the importer chose, with a confidence label (high, medium, low, or manual if you changed it) and an example value. Correct any wrong choice from the drop-down; — not imported — skips a field. A red note lists required fields still unmatched. For fields with a fixed list of values (such as priority), the page asks you to Translate any value it could not recognise, for example “Hot” to a priority. Under Options choose whether unmatched columns are kept as extra fields on the record or ignored (ignore them for anything private such as tax numbers), and whether 03/04/2025 means March 4 or 3 April. This only breaks ties; a column containing 25/04/2026 is read day-first automatically. Use Leave out rows where… to skip inactive items, test rows or other sites' data (for example Status is Inactive). Choose Check every row (nothing is saved yet) . Read the results (next section). When you are satisfied, choose Import N rows . On the final page, name and save the mapping with Save mapping . Next time, pick it under Saved mapping and choose Check with saved mapping . Reading the check Item Meaning Rows read Data rows found, after the header and blank lines. New records / Updates What would be created and what would be changed because the record already exists. A blank cell never erases an existing value. With warnings Rows that will import, but with an assumption you should know about (for example an ambiguous date order or an unknown unit that is kept as typed). With errors Rows that cannot be imported, each with its reason. Things these rows name that are not loaded yet For example “12 rows name 3 suppliers that are not loaded”. Load those first or fix the spelling. Preview The first rows as they will be saved, with create , update or skip . If there are errors, choose Download problems file . It contains the failing rows with their original values and a reason for each (and, for wide sheets, the exact column), so the owner of the data can fix their spreadsheet and you can check again. By default any error blocks the whole import . Ticking Import the good rows and skip the N with errors loads the good rows only and reports the rest. Nothing touches live records until you choose Import . You can run the check as often as you like. Checking and importing are separate steps: the import checks the rows again against current data when you press the button, so rows that became invalid in between are reported then. What can be imported, and in what order Follow the order of the Implementation planner : it locks a step until the data it depends on is loaded. In brief: Order Target (as named in the wizard) Matched on 1 Sites (properties, stores, plants); Departments / cost centers Site code; department code 2 Employees / technicians; People who sign in, with roles Employee number or legacy ID; work email 3 Assets / equipment register; Parts / spares master; Storerooms; Stock on hand (opening balances); Equipment parts lists; Meter readings Asset tag; part number; storeroom code; part and storeroom 4 Suppliers / vendors; Supplier price list; Open purchase orders; Supplier delivery history; Customers / accounts Supplier or customer code, or legacy ID 5 Bills of materials; Work centers; Routings (operations); Preventive maintenance plans Part, work center, asset tag 6 Chart of accounts; Opening balances (trial balance); Open customer invoices; Open supplier bills; Bank and card transactions; Spend history; Budget lines Account; invoice number; bank transaction id or date, amount and description 7 History: Maintenance history (legacy work orders); Downtime / state log; Qualifications and records; Calibration; SPC; Nonconformance and safety history; Timesheet history Legacy numbers and dates Other Leases and rental units; Condition limits and readings; Customer forecasts; Consumables usage; Sales items and opportunities; Earning codes; Expense categories Per target Zip Controlled documents (an upload of a zip of files plus an index sheet; opened from the plan step, with a dry-run check) Document number and revision The complete list, every field and the header spellings it recognises are shown on the matching screen. title: Implementation planner
text: The implementation planner turns “set the system up” into a list of steps with an owner, an order, a check and a progress bar. It is built around the data imports: loading a file moves its step on by itself, and a person then confirms the data is right. There are three parts: the fit interview (what should we switch on?), the plan (what do we load, and who does it?) and the practice copy (let us rehearse without touching real data). Administrators build the plan, assign owners, skip steps and unlock steps early. A person who has been made the owner of a step can start and verify that step, and sees Implementation in the menu while they have open steps. Everyone else cannot see the planner. The fit interview Open Admin → Fit interview . It is a business diagnosis in plain questions, about 60 in all. Questions that do not apply are not asked, so a manufacturer sees a different set from a landlord or a laboratory. The questions are grouped under headings: About the business: what the company does (makes products, maintains its own equipment or buildings, services other people's equipment, sells, runs restaurants or stores, rents property, runs a laboratory or cleanroom, sells professional services, office only, something else), sites, people, customers. Why now: the main reasons for looking at a new system, and what goes wrong most often today. How you earn and bill: fixed jobs, time and materials, service agreements, retainers, rent, tests; whether you bill hours, run projects, manage utilization, invoice retainers automatically, need a customer portal or a support queue with response targets. Equipment, stock and buying: equipment lists, stock and lots, scanning, purchase orders and quotes, with the size of each. Laboratories and cleanrooms: the kind of lab or cleanroom, samples and methods, the governing standard, room class, environmental monitoring, equipment qualification, chemical control and calibration. Proof and compliance: certifications, how often you are audited, change control, training records, record retention, electronic signatures and security reviews. People and money: timesheets, expenses, books, invoice volume and what you use today. Readiness: who will use it and on what devices, company sign-in, a named owner, who runs it afterwards, the state of your lists, how much history to bring and what it must connect to. Your own numbers: optional figures such as hours of downtime a month and what an hour costs, hours a week lost to paperwork, audit preparation days, scrap and rework, stock value, annual revenue and days to invoice. Goals and decision: what success looks like, when, who decides and what could stop it. Answer what you can. A partial set of answers is fine; you can come back. The page counts what you have answered. Choose Save answers and show the recommendation . Read What we suggest . It gives the recommended Implementation plan depth, the features to Show (each with a reason), those Worth considering and those Probably not needed yet , and a frank list under Not a fit yet (for example: no point-of-sale; scanning needs a connection; no payroll calculation or tax filing in the books). Read the diagnosis sections that follow: What your own numbers say , Measure these before you start , Your goals , How ready you are and You asked for things we have not built . Optionally choose Hide the features we did not recommend . This sets those features to Nobody (hidden) on the Features page and tells you how many were hidden. Features marked as shown or worth considering stay, and field service is never hidden by this button. You can undo any of it from Features . What your own numbers say If you typed numbers, the page multiplies them and shows the arithmetic next to each line: downtime hours a month times the cost of an hour times twelve, paperwork hours a week times the value of an hour times 52, audit preparation days times eight hours times the value of an hour, and the scrap figure as you gave it. Stock on hand and the cash waiting to be invoiced (annual revenue divided by 365 times the days to invoice) are shown separately as cash tied up. It also shows what each 10% of the yearly cost is worth. These lines show where money is exposed, using only your own figures. They are not a forecast of savings and nothing in the product promises a saving. Use them to choose what to measure first, then measure again after go-live. Measure these before you start For each problem you picked under What goes wrong most often today , the page names a measure and where the product reports it (for example unplanned downtime and MTBF in the Reliability report, on-time upkeep in PM compliance, days to invoice in the receivables aging report). Write down today's value before the first user signs in, so the comparison later is fair. How ready you are Plain flags: a named owner, someone to run it afterwards, the state of your lists, company sign-in, the risks you named, and whether the timeline suits the size. The level is ready , some work or needs groundwork . It is advice, and nothing is blocked. Things we have not built Some answers point to needs the product does not serve yet and has deliberately held: billing people's hours by client, projects with budgets and milestones, billable utilization, automatic retainer and subscription invoices, a customer portal, a support queue with response targets, point-of-sale, live connections to instruments, and records shaped to ISO/IEC 17025. The page lists them against your answers, and the answers are kept as evidence of demand. Operators can see the demand across all companies with npx tsx scripts/fit-demand.ts (add --json for a file). It lists each held need with the companies that asked, and is read-only. You can retake the interview at any time; the recommendation is recomputed from the saved answers. It is a starting point, not a rule: the system never changes anything without your pressing the button. The implementation plan

title: Archives and recovery
text: There are two separate safety nets, and it matters which one you reach for. Company archives are taken by the system itself and are for undoing mistakes inside one company: a record deleted by accident, a bad import that overwrote prices. Database backups are taken by whoever runs the server and are for disasters: a lost disk, a failed upgrade. This page covers both, but the archive screens are the part you use. Only an administrator sees Admin → Archives and restore . Rolling the whole company back needs two administrators. Company archives An archive is a full copy of the company's data from one consistent moment, saved as a compressed file with a checksum. The daily job takes one whenever the last is older than the interval, every 30 days by default , and keeps the latest 12 scheduled ones. The very first is taken by the first daily run after the company is set up. What an archive holds: every business record the company owns (work orders, stock movements, invoices, documents' records and so on), as database rows. What it does not hold: sign-in tokens, single sign-on secrets, people's unsaved form drafts, and the archives themselves. It holds the rows that refer to uploaded files, but not the file contents; those live in the server's storage folder and are protected by the server operator's file backups. Archives are stored in the same storage folder as uploaded files. If that folder is lost and not backed up, the archives go with it. That is why they do not replace database backups. The page The sentence at the top says how long ago the last archive was taken and when the next is due. The table lists each archive with when it was taken, its kind ( Scheduled , Taken by hand or Before a rollback ), the number of records, size and who took it. Actions per row: Bring records back , Download (a compressed file) and Roll back to this . Take an archive now Choose Archive now . Do this before any big import, bulk change or go-live cutover. On a test company with two years of history (about 20,000 ledger lines, 17.9 MB archive) it took about five seconds. Change the schedule Choose the button that says Schedule: every 30 days, keep 12 (it shows your current values). Set Archive every (days) (1 to 90) and Scheduled archives kept (1 to 120). Choose Save . Only scheduled archives are pruned. Archives taken by hand and the ones taken automatically before a rollback are kept until removed by the operator. Bring a record back Use this when a record was deleted or changed and you need the old version. Nothing else changes. On Archives and restore , choose Bring records back on the archive taken before the mistake. Under Kind of record pick the kind (each shows how many were archived). Optionally type a number, name or any text in Find and choose Search . The page says how many were deleted and changed since the archive, and shows up to 50 rows, deleted ones first. The column Since the archive shows Unchanged , Changed or Deleted . Tick the ones to bring back. Leave Include the records that belong to them (lines, steps, contacts) ticked unless you only want the top record. Choose Bring back N . Records are written back exactly as they were, with every business rule and reference still checked. If a record points at something that no longer exists, the restore is refused with a message, and nothing is half-restored. You can bring back at most 500 records at once. The result is recorded in the audit trail. Roll the whole company back This replaces everything entered since the archive . Use it only soon after a large mistake, such as a bulk import into the wrong place, and only if bringing records back would be too slow. What it keeps People, roles and their assignments, sign-in settings and tokens, the audit trail, record number counters (so numbers are never reused), the licence, and people's drafts are kept as they are now. Business records are replaced by the archive's. References left pointing at something that no longer exists are cleared. If the archive itself turns out to be inconsistent, nothing changes. Steps Administrator A chooses Roll back to this on the archive, types Why (at least five characters, for example “A bad import overwrote prices”) and chooses Ask a second administrator to confirm . The button is disabled, with an explanation, if the company has only one administrator: add another first. All administrators are notified. A banner, Rollback waiting for a second administrator , appears on the page. Administrator B reads the reason and chooses Confirm the rollback . Administrator A cannot confirm their own request, and either can Cancel it . A request not confirmed within 24 hours expires. The system first archives the present state (kind Before a rollback ), then replaces the business data in one step. The result is shown under Rollbacks : how many records were restored. On a test company with two years of history it took about 25 seconds. To undo a rollback , roll back again to the Before a rollback archive. Only one request can wait at a time. If the page says “this database does not let the platform suspend reference checks during a rollback; ask the platform operator to run it” (error rollback_unavailable ), your hosting database does not give the platform the privilege the rollback needs. Ask the server operator; nothing was changed. Also, work done by other people between the request and the confirmation is lost; tell them before you confirm. Archive messages Message Meaning the archive file does not match its checksum; it cannot be used ( archive_damaged ) The file changed or was damaged in storage. Use a different archive and tell the server operator. the archive has … records pointing at missing … records; nothing was changed ( archive_inconsistent ) The archive cannot be applied cleanly.
