title: Accounting connection
text: Invoices, supplier bills and expense reports have to end up in a set of books. This system gives you two real ways to do that: keep the books inside the system (the built-in books), or send bills and invoices to your outside accounting software as a file that you import there. There are no live connections to QuickBooks, Xero, Sage or similar software yet; the page says so. This page describes only what exists today. The screen under Admin → Accounting needs the integrations.manage permission, which the administrator and the bookkeeper role hold. Setting up the built-in books itself is done under Books and needs books.manage (the bookkeeper and administrator). The choices Choice What it is Use it when Built-in books A small-business ledger inside the system: chart of accounts, journal, bank statement import and matching, reconciliation, period lock, profit and loss, balance sheet, trial balance. Available in both Lite and Standard editions. The company has no accounting software, or wants one system. It is a good fit for small and mid-size companies. File export Approved supplier bills, issued customer invoices, credit memos and approved expense reports are written to CSV files (one file for each kind) that you download and import into any accounting system. Voids are included as VOID rows. The company keeps its books elsewhere. MOCK accounting system A simulated system inside the platform, for demonstrations and testing only. Nothing reaches a real accounting system. Only to demonstrate. Do not use in a real company. Only one connection is active at a time. To switch, disconnect the current one first (the built-in books refuse to start while another connection is active, and vice versa). The books do not include payroll processing, tax filing, multi-currency, consolidation, fixed-asset depreciation schedules or inventory valuation, in any edition. Set up the built-in books Open Books in the Finance section of the menu and choose Set up the books and fill in your main bank account (name, last four digits), the date and its balance on that date. You get a starter small-business chart of accounts that you can rename or add to. If the company is starting partway through, what customers still owe on invoices already issued and what the company owes on approved bills and expense reports come in as opening balances, and nothing posts twice. (This is also available later as Bring in open items in the books' settings.) The previous system's trial balance comes in through Admin → Data import as Opening balances (trial balance) ; bank statements as Bank and card transactions . See Importing data . Back on Admin → Accounting you will see a connection named Built-in books , with the counts of items sent, queued and needing attention. Entries in the journal never change; a correction is a reversal plus a new entry. Invoices, bills, expense reports and payments post to the journal when a sync runs (below). Connect a file export On Admin → Accounting , with no connection active, the page shows Connect . Choose File export: a CSV of approved bills to import into any accounting system . Under Approved invoices not yet sent choose Send them with the first sync (backfill everything already approved) or Only send invoices approved from now on . Choose Connect . Map your accounts (next section). To produce a file, choose Sync now . Files appear under Export files with the number of rows; choose Download and import the file into your accounting software. The table remembers when each was downloaded. Payment status does not come back from a file export; reconcile payments in your accounting software and record them in the platform's payables, or switch to the built-in books if you want one place. Map the accounts At the bottom of the page, Chart of accounts lists the kinds of invoice line the platform produces (travel expense, supplies, production materials, freight, capital projects and so on). For each, type your accounting system's Account number and Account name and choose Save . A row shows Mapped or Not mapped . A bill with an unmapped line waits in the queue until its account is mapped, so do this before the first sync. Running the sync Items are queued when something happens (a bill is approved, an invoice is issued or voided, an expense report is approved or reimbursed) and are sent when a sync runs. Sync now runs one and shows: “Sync finished: N sent, N will retry, N need attention, N payments received.” The sync runs once a day by itself. The daily job ( Scheduled jobs ) runs the sync for your company, with the built-in books or a connected provider, and records it there. If it cannot run, the Scheduled jobs page shows the reason and each administrator gets one notification a day. Once a day is the slowest the ledger can lag; for fresher figures press Sync now or ask the server operator to schedule npx tsx scripts/run-sync.ts (for example every five minutes; each run is safe to overlap). The sync queue Filter with All , Needs attention , Queued and Sent . Rows say what is being sent: Create bill , Void bill , Create customer invoice , Void customer invoice , Create employee expense bill or Expense reimbursed . A failed send retries automatically after 1, 5, 30, 120 and 720 minutes. After that it waits for a person and shows as Needs attention with the problem in the last column. The reminder Accounting sync problems tells integration administrators daily while any are parked. Choose Retry after fixing the cause (often an unmapped account). Retrying never creates a duplicate: each send carries a unique key. If you entered the item by hand in the accounting system, type how in the box (at least three characters, “Entered by hand as …”) and choose Mark resolved . Switching or disconnecting To move from the built-in books to external software, export the journal ( Books → Statements → Export journal ), import opening balances into the new system, then choose Disconnect on Admin →

title: Scheduled jobs
text: Once a day the server runs a housekeeping job for every company. It sends reminders, builds and sends email digests, syncs the accounting system, clears out expired working data, takes the company archive when one is due, and chases late reviews and similar items. You do not need to start it, but you should know how to check that it ran, because a silent failure means people stop getting reminders. Only an administrator sees Admin → Scheduled jobs . When it runs The server checks every minute. Once the configured hour has passed ( 06:00 UTC by default; the setting is DAILY_JOB_HOUR_UTC ) and today's job has not yet been claimed, it runs. It runs once per calendar day (UTC). If the server was down at 06:00, the job runs when it comes back up, as long as the day is not over. If several copies of the server run, the first to claim the day's row does the work and the others do nothing, so nothing is sent twice. The operator may switch the built-in scheduler off ( DAILY_JOB_ENABLED=false ) and use an outside scheduler instead. The page then says “The built-in daily job is switched off on this server; an external scheduler must run it.” What it does for your company Each company gets these steps, in order. A failure in one step is recorded and does not stop the next step; a failure in one company does not stop other companies. Step What happens Settings Reminders Sends every reminder that is due: maintenance, quality, safety, people, purchasing and finance, stock and sites, and periodic reviews. A quote about to expire gets one series of notices (7 days, 2 days, the day after), not two. Each is sent once per its dedupe rule, so a second run the same day does not duplicate. Reminders Digests Builds one email per person who wants email and has unread notifications not yet emailed (up to 50 items), then hands it to the mail server. A message that cannot be sent is kept and tried again by the next daily run. See the note on email below. Each person's notification settings; the mail server settings of the system Accounting sync If your company has an accounting connection (the built-in books or a provider), sends what is waiting, retries what failed earlier, and brings back payment status. Safe to repeat. If it cannot run, the page shows the reason and each administrator gets one notification a day. Accounting connection Retention Removes working data older than the periods you set: finished import rows, read and unread notifications, sent emails, unsaved form entries, expired tokens. It runs after the mail step so nothing is removed before it is sent. Data retention Archives Takes a company archive if the last is older than the interval (30 days by default), prunes scheduled archives beyond the number kept (12 by default), and expires rollback requests older than 24 hours. Archives Documents and others Brings released document revisions into force on their effective date; reminds about overdue document readings and specification reviews, late supplier RFQs and customer RFQs, unacknowledged change notices; sweeps temporary SOP changes (alerts to the owner at 14, 7, 3, 1 and 0 days, then daily once past the end date); generates service visits from agreements (only at sites licensed for field service); checks tool calibration for service vehicles. Reminders; Features; licence About the email digest Email is delivered only when the server has a mail server set up ( SMTP_HOST and the related settings; see Security and operations ). When it has not, the mail step writes each message as a file in the server's storage folder ( mail ); nothing reaches anyone , and the page says so in the Email card. People then receive reminders only in the notification bell. What has and has not been proven. The mail sender has been tested only against a stand-in mail server inside the test suite. It has not been run against a real provider or a real sending domain (an open decision for the owner; the plan step Outgoing email tracks it). After a provider is connected, press Send a test email to me and confirm the message arrives and is not filed as spam. Do not promise email reminders to users before you have seen that work. If a send fails, the message stays in the queue with the error and is tried again by the next daily run (a message is given up on after five failed attempts or two weeks, and administrators are notified). The job itself carries on with its other steps, and the failure is shown in the This company column. If the mail server cannot be reached at all, messages wait without using up their attempts. A person who turned email off after their digest was queued does not get it. The Scheduled jobs page The sentence at the top is the answer to “is it working?”: “The daily job last ran on 2026-10-22 (done); it runs every day at 06:00 UTC.” Good. “No daily job has run yet; the first runs at 06:00 UTC.” Normal on a new system. “The daily job has not run since …: check the server.” It last ran more than 36 hours ago. Tell the server operator. Under the sentence an Email card says whether the server can send email at all and how many messages are waiting or were given up on. It has the Send a test email to me button: it sends one message to your own address and reports Test email sent or the mail server's error text. The mail password is never shown; if the server echoes it, it is replaced by “[hidden]”. Without a mail server it tells you that nothing was sent. The table shows the last 14 days with Day , Result ( Done , Failed or Running ), Started by ( The schedule or A person ), Started and This company . The last column lists each step with what it did (for example Reminders: 12 sent , Accounting sync: delivered 3 ) and shows a step that failed in red with the reason. Runs started by a person show their name. A day shown as Failed because of another company does not mean yours failed; read your own column. Run it now Choose Run it now for thi

title: Security and operations
text: This page is for whoever installs, hosts and keeps the system running. It restates the operations runbook in readable form. Where the product has not settled something (hosting provider, mail service, identity provider), it says so rather than assuming. If you are the company administrator and someone else hosts the system, read it so you know what to ask them for. The shape of a deployment One Node 22 program (started with npm start ) that serves both the API and the web application. Build the web application first with npm run web:build . PostgreSQL 16 with two database logins . The owner login ( DATABASE_ADMIN_URL ) runs migrations and the daily jobs that must cross companies. The application login ( DATABASE_URL ) is the one every request uses, and it is restricted by row-level security (RLS): the database itself refuses to show one company's rows to another, whatever the program does. The two logins must be different. A persistent folder for uploaded files and company archives ( STORAGE_DIR ). There is no cloud object-storage option yet, so the folder must be on a persistent disk and be backed up together with the database. A reverse proxy or load balancer that provides https in front, with TRUST_PROXY=1 . Run a single copy of the program for now. The rate limiter keeps its counts in memory. The daily job is safe with several copies (the first to claim the day does the work), but limits would then be per copy. Restarting is safe at any time. Configuration Settings are environment variables. When NODE_ENV=production the server refuses to start if a required one is missing or unsafe, and logs a warning for the others. Variable Required What it is DATABASE_URL Yes The application login. Must not be the owner login and must not use a development password. DATABASE_ADMIN_URL Yes The owner login. APP_BASE_URL Yes The public https:// address. Used in links in emails and as the base of the single sign-on redirect address. SSO_SECRET_KEY Yes Encrypts the identity-provider client secrets stored in the database. At least 32 characters is checked at start; in use the program needs it to be 32 random bytes written in base64, so generate it with openssl rand -base64 32 . Keep a copy in your secret store, separate from the database backup : losing it means retyping every company's identity-provider secret. STORAGE_DIR Warned The persistent folder. Default ./.storage is lost when a container is replaced. TRUST_PROXY Warned 1 behind one proxy, so rate limits see real client addresses. METRICS_TOKEN Warned Turns on /metrics (404 otherwise) for a scraper presenting this token. SMTP_HOST Warned The outgoing mail server. If it is not set, email is not delivered : digests are written as files under STORAGE_DIR/mail and a warning is logged at start. Set it to send real email. SMTP_PORT , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASSWORD , SMTP_SECURE No Port (587; 465 with TLS), login (set both user and password or neither), and encryption: starttls (default; the connection must become encrypted before login), true (encrypted from the first byte) or false (none; only for a trusted relay on the same machine, and warned). The password is never logged, stored or shown. MAIL_FROM Warned The sender address on emails, for example Ops Platform <notifications@your-domain> . The domain needs SPF, DKIM and DMARC records set up with your mail provider. PORT , LOG_LEVEL No Listening port (3000), log level (info). MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES No Largest upload; default 50 MB. RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER , RATE_LIMIT_PER_ADDRESS No Requests per minute: 1200 per signed-in user, 120 per address for sign-in and public pages. 0 turns one off. DAILY_JOB_ENABLED , DAILY_JOB_HOUR_UTC No The built-in daily scheduler, on by default at 06:00 UTC. See Scheduled jobs . First deployment Create the two database logins and an empty database. The logins must exist before the migrations run, because the migrations grant rights to them. scripts/dev-db.sh shows the development equivalent. Install and build: npm ci , then npm run web:build . With DATABASE_ADMIN_URL set, run npm run db:migrate . Migrations only move forward and are recorded in a table called schema_migration . Start the server. Check GET /health (the program is up) and GET /ready (the database answers and every migration of this build is applied; it answers 503 otherwise). Create the first company and administrator with npx tsx scripts/create-company.ts --slug <slug> --name "<name>" --admin-email <email> (it needs DATABASE_ADMIN_URL ; add --edition lite for Lite, --help for every option). It wraps provisionTenant , adds the administrator and prints that person's first token once ; the token expires after 14 days unless you choose otherwise. There is deliberately no customer-facing screen for creating a company. A company is created as Standard or Lite , with its first site. Field service and later edition changes are switched with scripts/set-entitlement.ts (see Features and editions ). Sign in with that administrator's token and continue with Your first week . Upgrading Take a backup (see below). Also choose Archive now for each company if you can. Deploy the new build, run npm run db:migrate , restart. Until every migration has applied, /ready answers 503, so a load balancer holds traffic away from a half-upgraded copy. Rolling the program back is safe only while no new migration has been applied. Migrations cannot be reversed; after one has run, the way back is to restore the backup. Backup and recovery Database: the hosting provider's point-in-time recovery if it is managed; otherwise a nightly pg_dump (custom format) plus pg_dumpall --roles-only . Files: a snapshot of STORAGE_DIR taken at the same time. A restored database with older files (or the reverse) shows missing attachments, not corruption. Company archives are stored in the same folder. The secret: SSO_SECRET_KEY in the secret store. Drill: npx tsx scripts/backup-drill.ts (or npm run backup:drill ) dumps the database, restores it into a scrat

title: Glossary
text: This page explains the words and short forms you will meet in the menus and in this guide. Where a term is a general industry word, the meaning given is the everyday one; where the platform uses it in a particular way, that is said. Terms are in alphabetical order within each section. Use your browser's search ( Ctrl + F ) to find one. Maintenance, stores and production Asset A machine, vehicle, building system or other thing the company owns and keeps working, such as a press, a boiler or a walk-in cooler. Each has a tag (its number), a location and a history. See Assets . Availability The share of scheduled time a machine was able to run. Worked out from the states people record (running, down and why). Bill of material (BOM) The list of parts and quantities needed to make one finished product. Lines imported into the platform land on a draft revision that a person releases. Bin A shelf or location inside a storeroom where a part is kept. Condition reading A measured value logged against a piece of equipment, such as a cooler temperature, compared with its limits. An out-of-limit reading opens an excursion and a request. Corrective action Work done to fix the cause of a problem so that it does not come back. See CAPA. Downtime Time when a machine was not running, with a reason such as mechanical failure or waiting for material. Planned downtime (PM, setup) is separated from unplanned. Kit The set of parts a planned job needs, gathered ahead of time. A kit is “short” if some parts are not in stock. Lot A batch of a part received or made together, tracked as a group, usually with an expiry date. A serial number tracks one individual unit. Meter reading A count of hours, cycles or distance on a machine. Meter-based PM plans are triggered by it. Part A spare, material or finished item with a part number, a unit of measure and (optionally) a cost. PM (preventive maintenance) Scheduled upkeep done before something breaks, by calendar (every 30 days) or by meter (every 500 hours). A PM plan creates work orders when due. See Preventive maintenance . Production order An instruction to make a quantity of a product by following its routing. See Production orders . Repair or replace A report that compares what a machine has cost to keep running with the value of replacing it. Routing The ordered operations (steps) used to make a part, with the work center for each and its setup and run times. Scrap, rework Pieces made wrongly. Scrap is thrown away; rework is fixed and used. Shift log The note handed from one shift to the next, with facts compiled by the system and items carried forward. Space A unit, suite, room or common area inside a property, tracked as an asset of that kind. Storeroom A place where parts are kept and counted; every receipt, issue and count goes through the stock ledger. Stock ledger The permanent record of every movement of stock. Balances are the sum of the movements, and the ledger is never edited; corrections are new movements. Work center A machine group or manual station where an operation is done, with its working hours. Work order (WO) A job to repair, inspect or maintain something: who does it, what for, what parts and time were used and when it was verified. See Work orders . Quality, safety and change 8D “Eight disciplines”: a structured way of solving a problem in eight steps, from forming a team to preventing it from happening again. Run inside a CAPA. See CAPA and 8D . Audit (quality) A planned check of a process or supplier against a standard, with findings that become actions. Calibration Checking and adjusting a measuring instrument against a known standard. An instrument past its calibration date cannot be used for production measurements. CAPA Corrective and preventive action. A record that takes a problem from its root cause through fixes to a check that they worked. See CAPA and 8D . Containment Quick action to stop a problem spreading while the cause is found, such as holding suspect stock. Disposition The decision on nonconforming material: use as is, rework, scrap, return to supplier. ECN (engineering change notice) A notice that a design, specification or process has changed. In the platform, notices (ECN, PCN, supplier change, deviation, waiver, bulletin) are tracked from sent to acknowledged for each recipient. See Changes and notices . FMEA Failure mode and effects analysis: a worksheet that lists how something could fail, how bad it would be, how likely and how likely it is to be caught, to rank the risks. Incident, near miss An incident is a safety event where someone was hurt or something was damaged; a near miss could have been but was not. See Safety . ISO 9001 An international standard for quality management systems. Many customers ask to see evidence of it. MOC (management of change) A review-and-approve process for changes to equipment, processes or procedures before they go live, including a pre-startup check. See Changes and notices . NCR (nonconformance report) A record that something did not meet its requirements: a bad part, a missed step. It is contained, given a disposition and may lead to a CAPA. See Quality . PSSR (pre-startup safety review) A final check, part of a change, that everything is ready and safe before restarting. Qualification Proof that a person is authorised to do a type of work. Completing a course does not grant one; an authorised person does. Read-across Checking whether a problem found in one place could also exist elsewhere (another machine, line or site). SCAR Supplier corrective action request: asks a supplier to find and fix the cause of a problem with what they delivered. SPC (statistical process control) Charting measurements over time against calculated control limits to see when a process drifts before parts go out of tolerance. See SPC control charts . Temporary change A procedure change that is allowed for a stated period and then ends. See Temporary SOP changes . Buying, selling a

title: FAQ and troubleshooting
text: Find your symptom in the table that fits, then read across: what you see, the usual cause, and what to do. Messages are quoted as the system shows them. Some come with a short code in the technical details (for example forbidden ); administrators and the people who run the server use these codes, so they are listed too. If your problem is not here, note the exact wording and the reference number, if there is one, and ask your administrator. Signing in You see Why What to do “Your session has ended. Sign in again.” (401) Your sign-in expired (single sign-on sessions last 12 hours), you signed out in another window, or the token was revoked or never valid. Sign in again. What you were typing is kept as a draft in most forms. “single sign-on is not set up for example.com; ask your administrator, or sign in another way” (404 sso_not_configured ) Your email's domain is not in the company's list, or single sign-on is switched off. Administrator: add the domain and tick single sign-on is on . “<email> is not a user of <company>; ask your administrator to add you” (403 sso_no_user ), sometimes with “the provider did not confirm the email address” Nobody has added you, the email differs from the provider's, the user is inactive, or the provider does not send a verified-email claim. Administrator: check the people import and the email claims . “this sign-in has expired or was already used; start again” (401 sso_state ) More than 10 minutes passed, or the page was reloaded or used twice. Start from the sign-in page again. “the identity provider answered 4xx” or “did not return JSON” (502 sso_provider ) Wrong client secret or redirect address registered, or the provider is down. Administrator: compare the settings with the provider's; try again later. “the ID token …” (401 sso_token ) The provider's token failed a check: wrong client id, unsupported signing method, expired, or the server's clock is out by more than a minute. Administrator and server operator: check client id and server time. The token you pasted is refused with “invalid or expired token” The token is wrong, revoked, or the company has switched API tokens off. Use single sign-on, or ask the administrator whether tokens are on. A person or token that worked is suddenly refused (401 “invalid or expired token”) The account was disabled, the token was revoked or has reached its expiry, or the company switched API tokens off. Administrator: Admin → People and access . Check the person's status on Users and the token on Tokens (tick Show revoked and expired ); enable the account or issue a new token. “missing bearer token” (401) A script called the system with no token. Send Authorization: Bearer erp_… . Access and missing menus You see Why What to do “missing permission: work_orders.manage” (403 forbidden ) Your roles do not include that permission at that site. The permission name tells you what is needed. Look it up in the Permissions table ; ask your administrator for the right role at the right site ( scoping ). “<Feature> is turned off for your role. An administrator can turn it on under Admin → Features.” (403 feature_off ) An administrator has hidden that area from your role. Ask them to change Features . “This is part of the Standard edition. Your company uses Lite (books, invoicing, bills, expenses, policies and the intranet); an administrator can upgrade.” (403 edition ) The company's plan is Lite, which excludes that area. An upgrade is made by whoever operates your licence ( Lite and Standard ). “Field service is not licensed for this site” (402 module_not_licensed ) Field service is licensed per site and this site does not have it. Work at a licensed site, or ask for the licence to be extended ( Licences ). The Field service menu appears only if at least one site has it. “you cannot give ‘…’: you do not hold it …” (403 escalation ) You tried to give a role, put a permission in a company role, or issue a token for someone who holds more than you do, at that place. Ask an administrator who holds that access, or choose a role with fewer permissions. Only the Administrator permission itself is exempt. A menu entry you expect is not there No role of yours has the needed permission, the feature is hidden from your role, or the entry is for administrators only. Check the two rows above. Some entries show only with a certain permission, such as Reviews, Reminders or Implementation. You can see a list but not the records or buttons You have view but not manage , or your role is granted at a different site. Ask for the right role at the site. “you cannot approve your own timesheet”, “you cannot approve a request you raised”, “the person who captured an invoice cannot approve it” (422 invalid ) Separation of duties: a second person must sign. Ask another approver. In a company where you are the only possible signer and the licence allows it, self-approval is allowed and recorded. Too many requests, conflicts and the server You see Why What to do “Too many requests. Try again in N seconds.” (429 rate_limited ) You, or everyone behind your address, sent more requests than allowed in a minute. Wrong tokens count too. Wait the number of seconds shown. Use a different code, or find and edit the existing record. “overlaps an existing record” (409) Two records of the same kind may not overlap in time, such as two machine states in the same hours. text: A permission is one thing a person may do, such as approving a timesheet or releasing a production order. A role is a named bundle of permissions. This page lists all 89 permissions and, for each, the starter roles that hold it. It is generated from the product's permission list, so it matches what the system checks. How permissions work Every new company starts with 25 roles (listed below). The Administrator role holds every permission, including tenant.admin . A person is given a role at one site, on a group of sites, or at all sites (leave the site blank when granting). A permission only works at the sites where a role covering it was granted. See Sites and people and Roles and access . A person with several roles gets the combined permissions of all of them, site by site. Hiding a feature under Features removes that feature's permissions from the roles it is hidden from (the setting is cached for up to about 30 seconds). The permission is still in the role, but the system treats it as not held. Some actions are decided by a step in an approval chain rather than by a permission. Expenses and purchase requests are examples: the approver named in the rule can sign even without the matching manage permission. Nobody can approve their own timesheet or expense report (except in a single-person company where the licence allows it). The starter roles cannot be edited. An administrator can make company roles under Admin → People and access → Roles by ticking permissions from this list (only ones the administrator holds; tenant.admin is the exception). Company roles are not listed below, because every company has its own; the Roles tab shows them with their permissions. Lite has the starter roles only. To see what a particular person can do, add up the roles they were granted, then look each permission up here. The Administrator column is left out of the tables because the Administrator role holds everything.
